title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄序
皇上建極作人十有九年于茲文
明之化固宜漸被遐域茲試
也合提學副使毛〔衢〕所簡〔士〕
二千五百有奇而得七十人
文詞之彬蔚論議之精邃視
兩畿曷讓焉〔應春〕河洛之鄙
===
人也想慕蜀邦昔賢之風烈
久矣今得與學〔正石〕〔繼興〕教
諭姚〔文燁〕陳〔鑰〕史〔元中〕林〔入〕
〔紀〕沈〔一元〕楊〔琨〕聚大邦之瓌
瑰而盡觀之不其幸與方其
始入院也巡按御史王〔珩〕以
監臨重任求才大事宜胥矢
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄序

皇上建極作人十有九年于茲，文明之化固宜漸被遐域。茲試也，合提學副使毛〔衢〕所簡〔士〕二千五百有奇，而得七十人。文詞之彬蔚，論議之精邃，視兩畿曷讓焉？〔應春〕河洛之鄙人也，想慕蜀邦昔賢之風烈久矣。今得與學〔正石〕〔繼興〕、教諭姚〔文燁〕、陳〔鑰〕、史〔元中〕、林〔入〕〔紀〕、沈〔一元〕、楊〔琨〕，聚大邦之瓌瑰而盡觀之，不其幸與？方其始入院也，巡按御史王〔珩〕以監臨重任、求才大事，宜胥矢
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

It is now nineteen years since His Majesty established the supreme standard and began nurturing men of talent. The transforming influence of his cultivated rule should certainly by now have spread to distant regions. For this examination, more than 2,500 candidates selected by Mao Qu, Education Intendant and Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were assembled, and seventy were chosen. In the refinement and richness of their writing and the precision and depth of their arguments, how could they yield anything to the two metropolitan regions?

I, Yingchun, am an uncultivated man from the region of the Yellow and Luo Rivers. I have long admired the exemplary character and achievements of the former worthies of Shu. Now, together with Shi Jixing, an Instructor, and Yao Wenye, Chen Yue, Shi Yuanzhong, Lin Ruji [?], Shen Yiyuan, and Yang Kun, all Instructors, I have been able to gather the treasures of this great province and examine them all. Is this not good fortune?

When we first entered the examination compound, Wang Heng, the Regional Inspector, held that, given the weighty responsibility of supervision and the great undertaking of seeking talent, we should all make a solemn pledge …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
於神乃率提調官左布政使
李〔崧祥〕右叅政敖〔英〕監試官
副使柯〔相〕僉事蔣〔信〕及豫簡
諸執事之英藝檀陳詞以徼
神之聽蓋誠濘乎若上帝之
鑒觀于茲矣〔應春〕以是固已
知茲試也其必得真才矣夫
===
令何以爲爾多士勗乎惟爾
蜀邦自昔顯名之士遐軌邈
矣簡冊有稽馬多士稽古之
餘寧無曰吾邦有若神禹者
乎拯天下魚鼈之患至於三
過門而不入是汲汲於仁天
下者也有若司馬相如揚雄
punctuated:
於神，乃率提調官左布政使李〔崧祥〕、右叅政敖〔英〕、監試官副使柯〔相〕、僉事蔣〔信〕及豫簡諸執事之英，藝檀陳詞，以徼神之聽。蓋誠濘乎若上帝之鑒觀于茲矣。〔應春〕以是固已知茲試也，其必得真才矣。
夫令何以爲爾多士勗乎？惟爾蜀邦自昔顯名之士，遐軌邈矣，簡冊有稽馬。多士稽古之餘，寧無曰：「吾邦有若神禹者乎？拯天下魚鼈之患，至於三過門而不入，是汲汲於仁天下者也。有若司馬相如、揚雄」
translation_en:
…to the spirits. He then led the Proctors, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Songxiang and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Ao Ying; the Examination Monitors, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Ke Xiang and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Xin; and the outstanding men previously selected for the various examination duties, to approach the altar [?] and recite an invocation, seeking the spirits’ hearing. Their sincerity was such [?] that it seemed the Lord on High was watching over this very place. From this, I, Yingchun, already knew for certain that this examination would obtain men of true talent.
Now [?], how shall I exhort you, assembled scholars? The illustrious men of your land of Shu have left exemplary traces reaching far back into antiquity; these can be examined in written records [?]. As you scholars study the past, would you not say: “Did our land not have a man like the divine Yu? He rescued the people of the world from the calamity of becoming fish and turtles, even passing his own gate three times without entering. Such was his urgency in extending benevolence to all under Heaven. Were there not men like Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong…”

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
者乎子虛上林甘泉河東之
作詭麗極矣是以文章獵取
聲利者也近代有若張敬夫
者乎春風沂水有逸與焉是
希聖之流也又寧無曰禹之
功烈昭昭天壤敬夫雖未大
施用顧其幽馨曷可泯也彼
===
相如輩瞬息之聲利視此何
如邪夫是則然矣抑嘗就若
人而究其始否乎孟子曰雞
鳴而起孳孳爲善者舜之徒
也雞鳴而起孳孳爲利者跖
之徒也欲知舜與跖之分無
他利與善之閒也禹雖萬世
punctuated: 者乎？《子虛》《上林》《甘泉》《河東》之作，詭麗極矣，是以文章獵取聲利者也。近代有若張敬夫者乎？春風沂水，有逸與焉，是希聖之流也。又寧無曰：「禹之功烈，昭昭天壤；敬夫雖未大施用，顧其幽馨曷可泯也？彼相如輩瞬息之聲利，視此何如邪？」夫是則然矣，抑嘗就若人而究其始否乎？孟子曰：「雞鳴而起，孳孳爲善者，舜之徒也；雞鳴而起，孳孳爲利者，跖之徒也。欲知舜與跖之分，無他，利與善之閒也。」禹雖萬世
translation_en:
…such men? The compositions Rhapsody of Sir Vacuous (Zixu), Rhapsody on the Shanglin Park (Shanglin), Rhapsody on the Sweet Springs Palace (Ganquan), and Rhapsody on Hedong attain the utmost in extravagant splendor. These were men who used literary composition to hunt for fame and profit. In more recent times, was there someone like Zhang Jingfu? In the spring breeze beside the Yi River, he found an untrammeled delight [?]: he belonged among those who aspired to sagehood. And would you not also say: “Yu’s achievements shine brightly throughout heaven and earth. Although Jingfu never had much opportunity to put his abilities into practice, how could the quiet fragrance of his virtue be effaced? How does the fleeting fame and profit of Xiangru and his like compare with this?”
That is indeed so. But have you ever examined such men and investigated their initial impulses? Mencius said: “Those who rise at cockcrow and diligently pursue goodness are followers of Shun. Those who rise at cockcrow and diligently pursue profit are followers of Zhi. If you wish to know what distinguishes Shun from Zhi, it is nothing other than the difference between profit and goodness.” Although Yu, for ten thousand generations, …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
稱神要其心其始也惟孳孳
爲善耳相如葦則不免於孳
孳爲利嚮使能變其所趨將
不厭子虛甘泉諸作而爲董
仲舒正誼明道之論以與六
經竝傳乎一心義利之趨誠
弗可以弗辯也已是故惟其
===
爲義其進也必上爲君父下
爲生民而弗遑身圖世道用
楨焉惟其爲利其進也必惟
便利是圖上負君父而下誤
生民國家用否焉是故苟端
其趨如敬夫氏功烈不必如
禹而可以無愧於堯舜矣夫
punctuated:
稱神，要其心，其始也惟孳孳爲善耳。相如葦則不免於孳孳爲利。嚮使能變其所趨，將不厭子虛、甘泉諸作，而爲董仲舒正誼明道之論，以與六經竝傳乎？一心義利之趨，誠弗可以弗辯也已。
是故，惟其爲義，其進也必上爲君父，下爲生民，而弗遑身圖，世道用楨焉。惟其爲利，其進也必惟便利是圖，上負君父，而下誤生民，國家用否焉。是故，苟端其趨，如敬夫氏，功烈不必如禹，而可以無愧於堯舜矣夫！
translation_en:
… acclaimed as divine; yet, examining his heart, at the outset he merely strove diligently to do good. Xiangru and his ilk [?] could not escape striving diligently for profit. Had he changed the direction of his pursuits, would he not have tired of such compositions as “Sir Vacuous” (Zixu) and “Sweet Springs” (Ganquan), and instead produced discussions like Dong Zhongshu’s on rectifying righteousness and illuminating the Way, to be transmitted alongside the Six Classics? Whether the heart inclines toward righteousness or profit is truly a distinction that must be discerned.
Thus, when a man acts for righteousness, his advancement will necessarily serve his sovereign and father above and the people below. He will have no leisure to scheme for himself, and the moral order of the world will thereby gain support. When he acts for profit, his advancement will necessarily aim solely at his own advantage: above, he will betray his sovereign and father; below, he will lead the people astray. The state will thereby fall into decline. Thus, if one sets the direction of one’s pursuits aright, as did Master Jingfu, one’s achievements need not equal Yu’s for one to stand without shame before Yao and Shun!

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
〔應春〕以爾多士之文及茲當
道爲
朝廷求才之意而知爾多士必
皆真才也可以〔應春〕言爲贄
詞乎哉抑茲盛舉先事揆度
宏典裕需則巡撫右副都御
史李〔欽〕乃以進工部右侍郎
還京而巡撫右僉都御史劉
===
〔大謨〕適至飭舊敷新髦士作
氣其禮聘司衡恢拓程式則
肇於巡按御史董〔珊〕若工部
郎中戴〔時升〕則以公事至適
觀厥成其調度規防則右布
政使張〔聰〕左叅政郝〔世家〕右
punctuated:
〔應春〕以爾多士之文，及茲當道爲朝廷求才之意，而知爾多士必皆真才也。可以〔應春〕言爲贄詞乎哉？
抑茲盛舉，先事揆度，宏典裕需，則巡撫右副都御史李〔欽〕，乃以進工部右侍郎還京，而巡撫右僉都御史劉〔大謨〕適至，飭舊敷新，髦士作氣。其禮聘司衡，恢拓程式，則肇於巡按御史董〔珊〕。若工部郎中戴〔時升〕，則以公事至，適觀厥成。其調度規防，則右布政使張〔聰〕、左叅政郝〔世家〕、右
translation_en:
…I, Yingchun, judging from the writings of you assembled scholars and from the intention of the authorities here to seek talent for the court, know that you must all possess genuine talent. Might these words of mine, Yingchun’s, serve as an introductory offering?
As for this grand undertaking, advance planning and ample provision for the requirements of this great ceremony fell to Li Qin, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-chief. He then returned to the capital upon promotion to Right Vice Minister of Works, while Liu Damo, Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, arrived just then. Liu put existing arrangements in order and introduced new measures, inspiring the outstanding scholars. The courteous recruitment of examiners and the expansion of examination procedures originated with Dong Shan, Regional Inspector. Dai Shisheng, a Director in the Ministry of Works, came on official business and happened to witness its completion. Arrangements for resources and preventive measures fell to Zhang Cong, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Hao Shijia, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; and the Right…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
叅政侯〔緘〕左叅議潘〔恩〕右叅
議操〔松〕副使富〔好禮〕劉〔佐〕張
〔問之〕王〔莘〕僉事李〔禊〕薛〔甲〕方
〔定〕茍〔汝安〕周〔宗鎬〕陸〔時雍〕戒
嚴邏衛則都指揮僉事鄧〔斌〕
魯〔元忠〕若右布政使劉〔勲〕按
察使田〔秋〕僉事段〔續〕則先事
預勞以被擢去右叅議劉〔采〕
僉事潘〔瑞〕都指揮僉事沈〔一〕
〔元〕則先以奉
賀入
覲皆不可不書云
山西潞安府儒學教授李〔應〕
〔春〕謹序
punctuated:
叅政侯〔緘〕、左叅議潘〔恩〕、右叅議操〔松〕、副使富〔好禮〕、劉〔佐〕、張〔問之〕、王〔莘〕、僉事李〔禊〕、薛〔甲〕、方〔定〕、茍〔汝安〕、周〔宗鎬〕、陸〔時雍〕。戒嚴邏衛，則都指揮僉事鄧〔斌〕、魯〔元忠〕。若右布政使劉〔勲〕、按察使田〔秋〕、僉事段〔續〕，則先事預勞，以被擢去。右叅議劉〔采〕、僉事潘〔瑞〕、都指揮僉事沈〔一〕〔元〕，則先以奉賀入覲，皆不可不書云。
山西潞安府儒學教授李〔應〕〔春〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Administration Vice Commissioner Hou Jian; Left Administration Assistant Commissioner Pan En; Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Cao Song; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Fu Haoli, Liu Zuo, Zhang Wenzhi, and Wang Shen; and Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Li Xi, Xue Jia, Fang Ding, Gou Ru’an, Zhou Zonggao, and Lu Shiyong. Security precautions, patrols, and guards were the responsibility of Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Deng Bin and Lu Yuanzhong. Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Liu Xun, Surveillance Commissioner Tian Qiu, and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Duan Xu had contributed their efforts in advance of the examination but departed upon promotion. Right Administration Assistant Commissioner Liu Cai, Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Pan Rui, and Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Shen Yiyuan had earlier gone to court to offer congratulations and attend an imperial audience. All must be recorded here.
Preface respectfully composed by Li Yingchun, Prefectural School Professor of Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖十九年四川鄉試
監臨官
巡按四川監察御史王珩〔節甫直隸交河縣人 壬辰進士〕
提調官
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使李崧祥〔時望直隸貴池縣人 甲戌進士〕
四川等處承宣布政使司右參政敖英〔子發江西清江縣人 辛巳進士〕
監試官
四川等處提刑按察司副使柯相〔元卿直隸貴池縣人 丁丑進士〕
四川等處提刑按察司僉事蔣信〔卿實湖廣武陵縣人 壬辰進士〕
===
考試官
山西潞安府儒學教授李應春〔震卿河南河陰縣人 己卯貢士〕
河南開封府歸德州儒學學正石繼興〔克興浙江餘姚縣人 戊子貢士〕
同考試官
河南懷慶府武陟縣儒學教諭姚文燁〔在韜福建莆田縣人 壬午貢士〕
湖廣岳州府臨湘縣儒學教諭陳鑰〔啓特廣東潮陽縣人 甲午貢士〕
江西臨江府清江縣儒學教諭史元中〔良德浙江鄞縣人 辛卯貢士〕
浙江台州府天台縣儒學教諭林人紀〔肇脩福建莆田縣人 戊子貢士〕
江西臨江府新淦縣儒學教諭沈一元〔本乾福建閩縣人 甲午貢士〕
punctuated:
嘉靖十九年四川鄉試。

監臨官：
巡按四川監察御史王珩〔節甫，直隸交河縣人，壬辰進士〕。

提調官：
四川等處承宣布政使司左布政使李崧祥〔時望，直隸貴池縣人，甲戌進士〕。
四川等處承宣布政使司右參政敖英〔子發，江西清江縣人，辛巳進士〕。

監試官：
四川等處提刑按察司副使柯相〔元卿，直隸貴池縣人，丁丑進士〕。
四川等處提刑按察司僉事蔣信〔卿實，湖廣武陵縣人，壬辰進士〕。

考試官：
山西潞安府儒學教授李應春〔震卿，河南河陰縣人，己卯貢士〕。
河南開封府歸德州儒學學正石繼興〔克興，浙江餘姚縣人，戊子貢士〕。

同考試官：
河南懷慶府武陟縣儒學教諭姚文燁〔在韜，福建莆田縣人，壬午貢士〕。
湖廣岳州府臨湘縣儒學教諭陳鑰〔啓特，廣東潮陽縣人，甲午貢士〕。
江西臨江府清江縣儒學教諭史元中〔良德，浙江鄞縣人，辛卯貢士〕。
浙江台州府天台縣儒學教諭林人紀〔肇脩，福建莆田縣人，戊子貢士〕。
江西臨江府新淦縣儒學教諭沈一元〔本乾，福建閩縣人，甲午貢士〕。
translation_en:
Sichuan Provincial Examination, the nineteenth year of Jiajing (1540).

Supervising Official:
Wang Heng, Regional Inspector of Sichuan and Investigating Censor, courtesy name Jiefu, was a native of Jiaohe County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the renchen year.

Proctors:
Li Songxiang, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Shiwang, was a native of Guichi County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the jiaxu year.
Ao Ying, Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right of Sichuan, courtesy name Zifa, was a native of Qingjiang County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the xinsi year.

Examination Monitoring Officials:
Ke Xiang, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Yuanqing, was a native of Guichi County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the dingchou year.
Jiang Xin, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan, courtesy name Qingshi, was a native of Wuling County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate of the renchen year.

Examiners:
Li Yingchun, Prefectural School Professor of Lu’an Prefecture, Shanxi, courtesy name Zhenqing, was a native of Heyin County, Henan, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the jimao year.
Shi Jixing, Subprefectural School Director of Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Kexing, was a native of Yuyao County, Zhejiang, and a tribute student of the wuzi year.

Associate Examiners:
Yao Wenye, County School Instructor of Wuzhi County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan, courtesy name Zaitao, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute student of the renwu year.
Chen Yue, County School Instructor of Linxiang County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, courtesy name Qite, was a native of Chaoyang County, Guangdong, and a tribute student of the jiawu year.
Shi Yuanzhong, County School Instructor of Qingjiang County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Liangde, was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang, and a tribute student of the xinmao year.
Lin Renji, County School Instructor of Tiantai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, courtesy name Zhaoxiu, was a native of Putian County, Fujian, and a tribute student of the wuzi year.
Shen Yiyuan, County School Instructor of Xingan County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, courtesy name Benqian, was a native of Min County, Fujian, and a tribute student of the jiawu year.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
湖廣岳州府華容縣儒學教諭楊琨〔直隸定遠縣人辛卯貢士　用越府西桂林籍〕
印卷官
四川等處承宣布政使司經歷司經歷趙涣〔汝楫直隸涇縣人監生〕
四川等處提刑按察司經歷司經歷王來儀〔德召山東平陰縣人監生〕
收掌試卷官
成都府知府傅應祥〔德和江西進賢縣人丙戌進士〕
重慶府知府黄鳳翔〔冲宵雲南右衛籍浙江鄞縣人丙戌進士〕

順慶府同知程緒〔正甫，陝西寶雞縣人，癸未進士〕。

瀘州知州胡思忠〔進之，直隸桃源縣人，己丑進士〕。
嘉定州知州高登〔應明，貴州威清衛官籍，直隸儀真縣人，乙酉貢士〕。
成都府內江縣知縣李和芳〔仁父，湖廣公安縣人，戊戌進士〕。
保寧府南部縣知縣王炯〔幼明，貴州清平衛官籍，浙江嵊縣人，戊戌進士〕。

translation_en:
Yang Kun, Instructor of the Confucian School of Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a native of Dingyuan County, Zhili, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the xinmao year. The remaining annotation, “用越府西桂林籍,” appears garbled; it mentions registration in Guilin [?].

Officials Responsible for Printing Examination Papers:
Zhao Huan, courtesy name Ruji, was Registrar in the Registry of the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission. He was a native of Jing County, Zhili, and an Imperial University student.
Wang Laiyi, courtesy name Dezhao, was Registrar in the Registry of the Sichuan Provincial Surveillance Commission. He was a native of Pingyin County, Shandong, and an Imperial University student.

Officials Responsible for Collecting and Keeping Examination Scripts:
Fu Yingxiang, courtesy name Dehe, was Prefect of Chengdu. He was a native of Jinxian County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the bingxu year.
Huang Fengxiang, courtesy name Chongxiao, was Prefect of Chongqing. He was registered with the Yunnan Right Guard, was a native of Yin County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year.
Liu Shiyong, courtesy name Jina, was Prefect of Baoning. He was a native of Qi County, Henan, and a tribute student (gongshi) of the jiazi year.

Officials Responsible for Receiving Examination Scripts:
Cheng Xu, courtesy name Zhengfu, was Vice Prefect of Shunqing. He was a native of Baoji County, Shaanxi, and a metropolitan graduate of the guiwei year.
Xu Qiao, courtesy name Renfu, was Prefectural Judge of Mahu. He was a native of Lingbao County, Henan, and an Imperial University student.
Hu Sizhong, courtesy name Jinzhi, was Magistrate of Luzhou Subprefecture. He was a native of Taoyuan County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the jichou year.
Gao Deng, courtesy name Yingming, was Magistrate of Jiading Subprefecture. He held officer-household registration with Weiqing Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Yizhen County, Zhili, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the yiyou year.
Li Hefang, courtesy name Renfu, was Magistrate of Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture. He was a native of Gong'an County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Wang Jiong, courtesy name Youming, was Magistrate of Nanbu County, Baoning Prefecture. He held officer-household registration with Qingping Guard, Guizhou, was a native of Sheng County, Zhejiang, and was a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.
Wang Yi, courtesy name Ruheng, was Magistrate of Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture. He was a native of She County, Zhili, and a metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year.

Officials Responsible for Sealing Candidates’ Identifying Information:
Zhu Xianji, courtesy name Keming, was Magistrate of Mianzhou Subprefecture, Chengdu Prefecture. He held officer-household registration with Menghua Guard, Yunnan, was a native of Luanzhou, Zhili, and was a tribute student (gongshi) of the guiyou year.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:

punctuated:
成都府崇慶州知州何克明〔緝之，江西進賢縣人，戊子貢士〕。保寧府巴州知州陳有容〔仁甫，直隸休寧縣人，壬午貢士〕。成都府雙流縣知縣金梅〔用御，浙江歸安縣人，壬午貢士〕。重慶府巴縣知縣王瑞〔得賢，湖廣江夏縣人，壬午貢士〕。重慶府安居縣知縣謝恒〔惟一，江西新淦縣人，壬午貢士〕。雅州榮經縣知縣徐瀾〔道夫，雲南臨安衛籍，直隸武進縣人，壬午貢士〕。

謄錄官：
夔州府推官羅一清〔健之，直隸泰州人，監生〕。重慶府合州知州葉稠〔桂芳，江西南昌縣人，己卯貢士〕。保寧府劍州知州丁揖〔濟甫，貴州永寧衛籍，直隸清河縣人，己卯貢士〕。雅州知州陳一善〔與可，廣西柳州衛籍，馬平縣人，己卯貢士〕。嘉定州犍爲縣知縣盧鳳儀〔應韶，雲南大理衛人，乙酉貢士〕。順慶府西充縣知縣甯元伯〔仁甫，湖廣衡陽縣人，戊子貢士〕。保寧府巴州通江縣知縣紀立〔豫之，江西永豐縣人，乙酉貢士〕。

對讀官：
四川等處承宣布政使司理問所理問李巽〔惟中，湖廣沅陵縣人，監生〕。成都府通判徐璣〔在衡，貴州都勻衛籍，江西南城縣人，戊子貢士〕。潼川州知州張珩〔以正，江西南昌縣人，戊子貢士〕。
translation_en:
He Keming, Magistrate of Chongqing Department in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jizhi and was from Jinxian County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the wuzi year.
Chen Yourong, Magistrate of Ba Department in Baoning Prefecture, had the courtesy name Renfu and was from Xiuning County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.
Jin Mei, Magistrate of Shuangliu County in Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yongyu and was from Gui’an County, Zhejiang. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.
Wang Rui, Magistrate of Ba County in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Dexian and was from Jiangxia County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.
Xie Heng, Magistrate of Anju County in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Weiyi and was from Xingan County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.
Xu Lan, Magistrate of Rongjing County in Ya Department, had the courtesy name Daofu. He was registered in Lin’an Guard, Yunnan, and was originally from Wujin County in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was a tribute scholar of the renwu year.

Transcription Officials:
Luo Yiqing, Prefectural Judge of Kuizhou Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jianzhi and was from Tai Department in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was an Imperial University student.
Ye Chou, Magistrate of He Department in Chongqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Guifang and was from Nanchang County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the jimao year.
Ding Yi, Magistrate of Jian Department in Baoning Prefecture, had the courtesy name Jifu. He was registered in Yongning Guard, Guizhou, and was originally from Qinghe County in the directly administered metropolitan region; he was a tribute scholar of the jimao year.
Chen Yishan, Magistrate of Ya Department, had the courtesy name Yuke. He was registered in Liuzhou Guard, Guangxi, and was originally from Maping County; he was a tribute scholar of the jimao year.
Lu Fengyi, Magistrate of Qianwei County in Jiading Department, had the courtesy name Yingshao and was from Dali Guard, Yunnan. He was a tribute scholar of the yiyou year.
Ning Yuanbo, Magistrate of Xichong County in Shunqing Prefecture, had the courtesy name Renfu and was from Hengyang County, Huguang. He was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.
Ji Li, Magistrate of Tongjiang County in Ba Department, Baoning Prefecture, had the courtesy name Yuzhi and was from Yongfeng County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the yiyou year.

Proofreading Officials:
Li Xun, Judicial Examiner in the Judicial Examination Office of the Sichuan Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Weizhong and was from Yuanling County, Huguang. He was an Imperial University student.
Xu Ji, Assistant Prefect of Chengdu Prefecture, had the courtesy name Zaiheng. He was registered in Duyun Guard, Guizhou, and was originally from Nancheng County, Jiangxi; he was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.
Zhang Heng, Magistrate of Tongchuan Department, had the courtesy name Yizheng and was from Nanchang County, Jiangxi. He was a tribute scholar of the wuzi year.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
蘧伯玉使人於孔子孔子與之坐而問焉
曰夫子何爲對曰夫子欲寡其過而未
能也使者出子曰使乎使乎
其次致曲曲能有誠誠則形形則著著則
明明則動動則變變則化唯天下至誠
爲能化
詩云迨天之未陰雨徹彼桑土綢繆牖戶
===
今此下民或敢侮予孔子曰爲此詩者
其知道乎能治其國家誰敢侮之
易
大哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也六爻發揮
旁通情也時乘六龍以御天也雲行雨
施天下平也
天地節而四時成節以制度不傷財不害
民
天地設位而易行乎其中矣成性存存道
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

蘧伯玉使人於孔子，孔子與之坐而問焉，曰：「夫子何爲？」對曰：「夫子欲寡其過而未能也。」使者出，子曰：「使乎！使乎！」

其次致曲，曲能有誠，誠則形，形則著，著則明，明則動，動則變，變則化，唯天下至誠爲能化。

詩云：「迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖戶。今此下民，或敢侮予？」孔子曰：「爲此詩者，其知道乎！能治其國家，誰敢侮之？」

易

大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。六爻發揮，旁通情也。時乘六龍，以御天也。雲行雨施，天下平也。

天地節而四時成，節以制度，不傷財，不害民。

天地設位，而易行乎其中矣。成性存存，道
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Qu Boyu sent a messenger to Confucius. Confucius sat with him and asked, “What is your master doing?” He replied, “My master wishes to lessen his faults but has not yet succeeded.” After the messenger left, the Master said, “What a messenger! What a messenger!”

Next comes bringing particular aspects of one's goodness to full development. Through these particular aspects, sincerity can be attained. Sincerity takes outward form; taking form, it becomes manifest; becoming manifest, it shines forth; shining forth, it moves others; moving others, it brings change; bringing change, it effects transformation. Only the utmost sincerity under Heaven can effect transformation.

The Book of Odes says: “Before the sky clouds over and rain falls, I gather mulberry roots and bind up my window and door. Now, would any of the people below dare to insult me?” Confucius said, “Did not the author of this ode understand the Way! If one can govern one's state and household well, who would dare to insult one?”

Book of Changes

Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, it is pure, unmixed, and refined. Its six lines unfold their significance, comprehensively communicating the circumstances they embody. At the proper times, it rides the six dragons to direct Heaven. Clouds move and rain falls, and all under Heaven is brought into harmony.

Heaven and Earth observe limits, and the four seasons are thereby established. Through regulation by institutions and measures, wealth is not depleted and the people are not harmed.

Heaven and Earth take their appointed positions, and change operates between them. One's fully realized nature is continually preserved; the Way …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
義之門
分陰分陽迭用柔剛故易六位而成章
書
帝曰疇若予工僉曰垂哉帝曰俞咨垂汝
共工垂拜稽首讓于殳斨暨伯與帝曰
俞往哉汝諧帝曰疇若予上下草木鳥
獸僉曰益哉帝曰俞咨益汝作朕虞益
拜稽首讓于朱虎熊羆帝曰俞往哉汝
諧
===
非知之艱行之惟艱王忱不艱允協于先
王成德
茲乃允惟王正事之臣茲亦惟天若元德
永不忘在王家
欽哉永弼乃后于彝憲
詩
采采芣苢薄言采之采采芣苢薄言有之
薄伐玁狁至于大原文武吉甫萬邦爲憲
泂酌彼行潦挹彼注茲可以餴饎豈弟君
punctuated:
義之門。
分陰分陽，迭用柔剛，故易六位而成章。

書
帝曰：「疇若予工？」僉曰：「垂哉！」帝曰：「俞！咨，垂，汝共工。」垂拜稽首，讓于殳、斨暨伯與。帝曰：「俞！往哉，汝諧。」帝曰：「疇若予上下草木鳥獸？」僉曰：「益哉！」帝曰：「俞！咨，益，汝作朕虞。」益拜稽首，讓于朱、虎、熊、羆。帝曰：「俞！往哉，汝諧。」
非知之艱，行之惟艱。王忱不艱，允協于先王成德。
茲乃允惟王正事之臣，茲亦惟天若元德，永不忘在王家。
欽哉！永弼乃后于彝憲。

詩
采采芣苢，薄言采之。采采芣苢，薄言有之。
薄伐玁狁，至于大原。文武吉甫，萬邦爲憲。
泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注茲，可以餴饎。豈弟君
translation_en:
…the gateway to righteousness.

Yin and yang are distinguished, and yielding and firmness are employed in alternation; thus the six positions of the Changes form an ordered pattern.

Book of Documents

The emperor said, “Who can oversee my works?” All replied, “Chui!” The emperor said, “Yes! Listen, Chui: you shall be Minister of Works.” Chui bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Shu, Qiang, and Bo Yu. The emperor said, “Yes! Go and undertake it; you will bring things into harmony.” The emperor said, “Who can oversee for me the grasses, trees, birds, and beasts of the highlands and lowlands?” All replied, “Yi!” The emperor said, “Yes! Listen, Yi: you shall be my Forester.” Yi bowed and knocked his head to the ground, yielding the appointment to Zhu, Hu, Xiong, and Pi. The emperor said, “Yes! Go and undertake it; you will bring things into harmony.”

Knowing is not difficult; putting knowledge into practice is difficult. If the king is sincere, it will not be difficult, and he will truly accord with the perfected virtue of the former kings.

These were indeed the ministers who set the king’s affairs in order; these, too, were men whose great virtue Heaven favored. They will never be forgotten in the royal house.

Be reverent! Always assist your sovereign in adhering to the enduring statutes.

Book of Odes

Thickly grows the plantain; let us gather it. Thickly grows the plantain; let us take it in.

They attacked the Xianyun, reaching as far as Dayuan. Jifu, accomplished in civil and military affairs, is a model for the myriad states.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
子民之父母泂酌彼行潦挹彼注玆可
以濯罍豈弟君子民之攸歸泂酌彼行
潦挹彼注玆可以濯溉豈弟君子民之
攸塈
天命多辟設都于禹之績歲事來辟勿予
禍適稼穡匪解
春秋
冬宋人取長葛〔隱公六年〕
秋大水〔桓公元年六月雨僖公三年〕
===
夏四月己巳晉侯齊師宋師秦師及楚人
戰于城濮楚師敗績〔僖公二十八年〕會
于蕭魚〔襄公十一年〕
吳入州來〔成公七年〕戊辰吳敗頓胡沈蔡
陳許之師于雞父〔昭公二十有三年〕冬
吳滅巢〔昭公二十有四年〕庚辰吳入郢
〔定公四年〕
禮記
在朝言禮問禮對以禮
punctuated:
子，民之父母。泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注玆，可以濯罍。豈弟君子，民之攸歸。泂酌彼行潦，挹彼注玆，可以濯溉。豈弟君子，民之攸塈。
天命多辟，設都于禹之績。歲事來辟，勿予禍適，稼穡匪解。
春秋
冬，宋人取長葛。〔隱公六年〕
秋，大水。〔桓公元年。六月，雨。僖公三年〕
夏，四月己巳，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮，楚師敗績。〔僖公二十八年〕會于蕭魚。〔襄公十一年〕
吳入州來。〔成公七年〕戊辰，吳敗頓、胡、沈、蔡、陳、許之師于雞父。〔昭公二十有三年〕冬，吳滅巢。〔昭公二十有四年〕庚辰，吳入郢。〔定公四年〕
禮記
在朝言禮，問禮，對以禮。
translation_en:
…the gentleman is the father and mother of the people. Draw that standing rainwater from afar; ladle it out there and pour it in here: it can be used to wash wine jars. The gracious gentleman is the one to whom the people turn. Draw that standing rainwater from afar; ladle it out there and pour it in here: it can be used for washing and rinsing. The gracious gentleman is the one in whom the people find rest.
Heaven commanded the many rulers to establish their capitals in the lands brought under cultivation by Yu. Come each year to attend upon the sovereign. Do not bring calamity or blame upon me; be unremitting in sowing and reaping.
Spring and Autumn Annals
In winter, the men of Song took Changge. 〔Sixth year of Duke Yin.〕
In autumn, there was a great flood. 〔First year of Duke Huan. In the sixth month, it rained. Third year of Duke Xi.〕
In summer, on the jisi day of the fourth month, the Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought against the men of Chu at Chengpu. The army of Chu was routed. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi.〕 They met at Xiaoyu. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xiang.〕
Wu entered Zhoulai. 〔Seventh year of Duke Cheng.〕 On the wuchen day, Wu defeated the armies of Dun, Hu, Shen, Cai, Chen, and Xu at Jifu. 〔Twenty-third year of Duke Zhao.〕 In winter, Wu destroyed Chao. 〔Twenty-fourth year of Duke Zhao.〕 On the gengchen day, Wu entered Ying. 〔Fourth year of Duke Ding.〕
Book of Rites
At court, speak of ritual propriety, inquire about ritual propriety, and reply in accordance with ritual propriety.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
趨以采齊行以肆夏周還中規折還中矩
進則揖之退則揚之然後玉鏘鳴也
唯君子爲能知樂是故審聲以知音審音
以知樂審樂以知政而治道備矣是故
不知聲者不可與言音不知音者不可
與言樂知樂則幾於禮矣禮樂皆得謂
之有德德者得也
故明乎其節之志以不失其事則功成而
德行立
===
第貳場
論
君子依乎中庸
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢以汲黯爲主爵都尉詔〔建元六年〕
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕
擬宋仁宗幸後苑觀刈麥輔臣
賀表〔皇祐元年〕
判語〔五條〕
punctuated:
趨以《采齊》，行以《肆夏》，周還中規，折還中矩。進則揖之，退則揚之，然後玉鏘鳴也。
唯君子爲能知樂。是故審聲以知音，審音以知樂，審樂以知政，而治道備矣。是故不知聲者，不可與言音；不知音者，不可與言樂。知樂則幾於禮矣。禮樂皆得，謂之有德。德者，得也。
故明乎其節之志，以不失其事，則功成而德行立。
第貳場
論
君子依乎中庸。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢以汲黯爲主爵都尉詔〔建元六年〕。
擬唐以魏徵爲太子太師誥〔貞觀十六年〕。
擬宋仁宗幸後苑觀刈麥，輔臣賀表〔皇祐元年〕。
判語〔五條〕
translation_en:
When moving briskly, one keeps time with “Gathering Shepherd’s Purse” (Cai Qi); when walking, with “Si Xia.” Circular turns conform to the compass, and angular turns to the carpenter’s square. On advancing, one bows with clasped hands; on withdrawing, one raises them. Only then do the jade pendants ring harmoniously.
Only the gentleman can understand music. Thus, by examining sounds, one comes to understand musical tones; by examining musical tones, one comes to understand music; and by examining music, one comes to understand government. The Way of governing is thereby complete. Thus, one cannot discuss musical tones with someone who does not understand sounds, nor discuss music with someone who does not understand musical tones. Understanding music brings one close to ritual propriety. To have attained both ritual propriety and music is called possessing virtue. Virtue means attainment.
Thus, if one understands the purpose of its prescribed observances and does not fail in carrying them out, achievement is completed and virtuous conduct established.
Second Session
Discourse
“The gentleman abides by the Mean.”
Edicts, Proclamations, and Memorials 〔One topic within this category [?].〕
Compose an edict in the voice of the Han emperor appointing Ji An Commandant in Charge of Noble Ranks. 〔Sixth year of Jianyuan.〕
Compose a proclamation in the voice of the Tang emperor appointing Wei Zheng Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. 〔Sixteenth year of Zhenguan.〕
Compose a congratulatory memorial in the voice of the chief ministers on Emperor Renzong of Song’s visit to the rear palace gardens to observe the wheat harvest. 〔First year of Huangyou.〕
Legal Judgments 〔Five items.〕

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:

第叁場
策五道
問周公無逸之訓七月之詩此有周文武
盛德大業之原以揆諸前代迪哲之主
所以克祈天永命者何莫由斯道也顧
帝王之學淵源莫測神契於千載之下
詎不難哉恭惟我
===
皇上夙膺景命嗣大歷服無逸之殿豳風之亭
皆非有所效慕因襲而爲之者謂非
淵默神衷洞契千古其必無是也不知
聖心獨契之妙亦有可窺測而言之者歟有謂
聖賢畏天命而悲人窮者夫聖賢胡獨
於人窮而悲邪無亦其心慊有不容已
punctuated:
增减官文書。
私借官車船。
乘輿服御物。
宿衛人兵仗。
略人略賣人。

第叁場
策五道

問：周公《無逸》之訓、《七月》之詩，此有周文武盛德大業之原。以揆諸前代迪哲之主，所以克祈天永命者，何莫由斯道也？顧帝王之學，淵源莫測，神契於千載之下，詎不難哉？恭惟我皇上夙膺景命，嗣大歷服，無逸之殿、豳風之亭，皆非有所效慕因襲而爲之者。謂非淵默神衷洞契千古，其必無是也。不知聖心獨契之妙，亦有可窺測而言之者歟？有謂聖賢畏天命而悲人窮者，夫聖賢胡獨於人窮而悲邪？無亦其心慊有不容已
translation_en:
Adding to or deleting from official documents.
Privately lending official carts and boats.
Articles for the emperor’s conveyances, clothing, and personal use.
Weapons of palace guards.
Abducting persons and selling abducted persons.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: The Duke of Zhou’s admonition in “Against Idleness” and the poem “The Seventh Month” are the source of the abundant virtue and great achievements of Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou. Judging by the enlightened rulers of earlier ages, how could any have succeeded in seeking Heaven’s enduring mandate except by following this way? Yet the learning of emperors and kings has unfathomable depths and origins. Is it not difficult to attain spiritual accord with it a thousand years later?

We reverently consider how Our Emperor early received the glorious mandate and succeeded to the great imperial charge. The Hall of No Idleness and the Pavilion of the Airs of Bin were certainly not built merely out of admiration for earlier examples or adherence to precedent. Without his profound, silent imperial mind penetrating the ages in spiritual accord, these surely could not have come into being. Might the wondrous understanding uniquely attained by the sagely mind nevertheless be discerned and expressed in words?

It has been said that sages and worthies stand in awe of Heaven’s mandate and grieve over the people’s distress. Why do sages and worthies grieve particularly over the people’s distress? Might it be that a feeling of unease in their hearts [?] cannot be restrained…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
歟孔子於大易發明聖人之學曰知崇
禮卑崇效天卑法地夫天廣大高明之
極也惟聖人之知如之故能探
聖心廣大高明之極而後知我
皇上之有取乎詩書者蓋出於聰明睿知之所
照臨彼區區希慕往迹而爲之者皆不
足道也此豈非執事之預有聞於諸士
者乎幸毋曰帝王之學非韋布士可得
而窺也
===
問孟子曰我非堯舜之道不敢陳於王前
故齊人莫如我敬王也然伊傅告君不
曰堯舜而曰烈祖之成德先王之成憲
周公告君不曰堯舜而曰儀刑文王萬
邦作孚孔子告君不曰堯舜而曰文武
之政布在方策其人存則其政舉豈伊
傅周孔於堯舜之道有不嘉樂之邪將
薄其君不足與有爲邪抑時異勢殊無
徵不信不可專泥於古邪不然則是伊
punctuated:
歟？孔子於《大易》發明聖人之學曰：「知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。」夫天，廣大高明之極也，惟聖人之知如之，故能探聖心廣大高明之極，而後知我皇上之有取乎《詩》《書》者，蓋出於聰明睿知之所照臨。彼區區希慕往迹而爲之者，皆不足道也。此豈非執事之預有聞於諸士者乎？幸毋曰帝王之學非韋布士可得而窺也。

問：孟子曰：「我非堯舜之道，不敢陳於王前，故齊人莫如我敬王也。」然伊傅告君，不曰堯舜，而曰「烈祖之成德，先王之成憲」；周公告君，不曰堯舜，而曰「儀刑文王，萬邦作孚」；孔子告君，不曰堯舜，而曰「文武之政，布在方策，其人存，則其政舉」。豈伊傅周孔於堯舜之道有不嘉樂之邪？將薄其君不足與有爲邪？抑時異勢殊，無徵不信，不可專泥於古邪？不然，則是伊
translation_en:
…? Confucius elucidated the learning of the sage in the Book of Changes, saying: “Knowledge is lofty; ritual is humble. Loftiness emulates Heaven; humility models itself on Earth.” Heaven is the utmost in breadth, greatness, height, and brightness. Only the sage’s knowledge resembles it. Thus one can fathom the utmost breadth, greatness, height, and brightness of the imperial mind, and only then understand that what Our Emperor draws from the Book of Odes and the Book of Documents proceeds from the illumination of his intelligence and sagely wisdom. Those who merely admire the traces of the past and act in imitation of them are scarcely worth mentioning. Is this not something you, sir, have already heard from the scholars? Please do not say that the learning of emperors and kings lies beyond the insight of scholars clad in plain cloth.

Question: Mencius said: “Unless it accords with the Way of Yao and Shun, I dare not set it forth before the king. Thus no one in Qi respects the king as I do.” Yet when Yi Yin and Fu Yue instructed their rulers, they spoke not of Yao and Shun but of “the perfected virtue of the illustrious ancestor” and “the established statutes of the former kings.” When the Duke of Zhou instructed his ruler, he spoke not of Yao and Shun but said: “Take King Wen as your model, and the myriad states will place their trust in you.” When Confucius instructed a ruler, he spoke not of Yao and Shun but said: “The government of Kings Wen and Wu is set out on the writing tablets. When the right men are present, their government is put into practice.” Could Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius have failed to esteem and delight in the Way of Yao and Shun? Or did they think so little of their rulers that they considered them incapable of achievement? Or was it because times and circumstances differed, and because what lacks corroboration commands no credence, so that one must not cling exclusively to antiquity? If not, then Yi Yin…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
傳周孔之敬其君不如孟子矣諸生行
將有事君之責不可無歸一之說也頤
聞焉
問士君子行己立身自有法度出處進退
義命攸存惟夫情或外徇是故行鮮協
中稽之漢史自高帝鄙薄儒生士多衒
鬻廉恥日喪卒致頌莽貢符一朝成羣
國何賴焉光武鑒切往弊物色隱逸褒
表風節而中世名士輩出清議是尚陵
===
夷至於桓靈以後國勢奄奄羣狡睥睨
神器猶未敢肆然掩取者諸君子維持
力也說者乃謂東漢尚節義不若西漢
何歟清議可尚也尋激而爲黨錮之禍
說者謂諸賢有以取之然歟否歟人亦
有言名節之稱起于衰世然則盛世士
人固不貴以名節自命歟諸賢之中當
時亦有見幾明哲獲免餘波之及君子
與之然則保身之道固當若是歟至宋
punctuated:
傳、周、孔之敬其君，不如孟子矣。諸生行將有事君之責，不可無歸一之說也。頤聞焉。

問：士君子行己立身，自有法度；出處進退，義命攸存。惟夫情或外徇，是故行鮮協中。稽之漢史，自高帝鄙薄儒生，士多衒鬻，廉恥日喪，卒致頌莽貢符，一朝成羣，國何賴焉？光武鑒切往弊，物色隱逸，褒表風節，而中世名士輩出，清議是尚。陵夷至於桓靈以後，國勢奄奄，羣狡睥睨神器，猶未敢肆然掩取者，諸君子維持力也。說者乃謂東漢尚節義不若西漢，何歟？清議可尚也，尋激而爲黨錮之禍，說者謂諸賢有以取之，然歟否歟？人亦有言，名節之稱起于衰世，然則盛世士人固不貴以名節自命歟？諸賢之中，當時亦有見幾明哲，獲免餘波之及，君子與之，然則保身之道固當若是歟？至宋
translation_en:
…the reverence that Fu Yue [?], the Duke of Zhou, and Confucius showed their rulers would fall short of that shown by Mengzi. You students will soon bear the responsibility of serving your ruler; you must have an explanation that reconciles these views. I would hear it [?].

Question: Men of learning and virtue have their own standards for conducting themselves and establishing their character. In taking office or remaining in retirement, advancing or withdrawing, moral duty and Heaven’s decree are at stake. Yet their feelings sometimes yield to external influences, and thus their conduct seldom accords with the proper mean. Examining the histories of the Han, we find that, after Emperor Gao treated Confucian scholars with contempt, many scholars flaunted and sold their talents. Integrity and a sense of shame declined daily, until crowds sprang up to praise Wang Mang and present auspicious tokens to him. What support could the state find in such men?

Emperor Guangwu, taking the earlier abuses deeply to heart as a warning, sought out recluses and honored moral integrity. By the middle of the dynasty, eminent scholars appeared in succession, and principled public criticism was esteemed. As decline continued into the period after Emperors Huan and Ling, the state’s strength ebbed, and a host of schemers eyed the imperial throne. That they still did not dare brazenly seize it was owing to these gentlemen’s efforts to sustain the dynasty. Yet commentators say that the Eastern Han fell short of the Western Han in its esteem for integrity and righteousness. Why?

Principled public criticism deserves esteem, yet before long it became so heated that it led to the calamity of the partisan prohibitions. Commentators say that these worthy men helped bring this upon themselves. Is that so or not? It has also been said that acclaim for reputation and integrity arises in an age of decline. Does this mean that scholars in a flourishing age should not prize defining themselves by reputation and integrity?

Among these worthy men were some who discerned the first signs of trouble and, through clear-sighted wisdom, escaped its repercussions. Gentlemen approve of them. Does this mean that the proper way to preserve oneself must indeed be like this? When it came to the Song…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
儒追論其事以諸賢分入仲由顏子二
科其果爲定論歟迨及兩晉士遂矯枉
過正一時波流風靡賤名檢鄙居正以
清談爲高致以勤事爲俗流禮法刑政
蕩然廢壞國亦隨之果孰爲之倡歟伊
欲士大夫以名節忠義爲本以正直忠
厚爲心上不爲東漢之矯亢下不爲西
漢兩晉之卑陋之浮靡折中之道又不
屑爲胡廣之中庸聖賢居身之所珍固
===
自有在試爲我籌之
問天下之不易言者性也孟子後孔子而
生獨曰性善豈固有所受之云乎性相
近習相遠上智下愚不移固孔子之言
也然則其說得無與相戾歟先儒以孟
子發明性善其功配禹先是果未有啓
其端者歟自張子有形而後有氣質之
性之說朱子因之嗣是談性學者皆以
爲無復遺論矣不知人性果有二歟且
punctuated:
儒追論其事，以諸賢分入仲由、顏子二科，其果爲定論歟？迨及兩晉，士遂矯枉過正，一時波流風靡，賤名檢，鄙居正，以清談爲高致，以勤事爲俗流，禮法刑政蕩然廢壞，國亦隨之，果孰爲之倡歟？伊欲士大夫以名節忠義爲本，以正直忠厚爲心，上不爲東漢之矯亢，下不爲西漢兩晉之卑陋之浮靡，折中之道又不屑爲胡廣之中庸，聖賢居身之所珍固自有在，試爲我籌之。
問：天下之不易言者，性也。孟子後孔子而生，獨曰性善，豈固有所受之云乎？「性相近，習相遠」，「上智下愚不移」，固孔子之言也。然則其說得無與相戾歟？先儒以孟子發明性善，其功配禹，先是果未有啓其端者歟？自張子「有形而後有氣質之性」之說，朱子因之，嗣是談性學者皆以爲無復遺論矣。不知人性果有二歟？且
translation_en:
…scholars of the Song retrospectively discussed these events and assigned the worthies to two categories, those of Zhong You and Master Yan. Is this indeed a definitive judgment? By the time of the Western and Eastern Jin, scholars had overcorrected these faults. Swept along by the prevailing fashion, they disparaged reputation and disciplined conduct, disdained upright living, regarded pure conversation as a lofty pursuit, and dismissed diligent service as vulgar. Ritual, law, punishments, and government fell into utter ruin, and the state followed them. Who, indeed, initiated this trend? If we wish scholar-officials to take moral reputation, integrity, loyalty, and righteousness as their foundation, and uprightness, loyalty, and generosity as their guiding disposition, avoiding at one extreme the affected hauteur of the Eastern Han and at the other the baseness of the Western Han and the frivolity of the two Jin dynasties, while seeking a balanced course that disdains Hu Guang’s so-called adherence to the mean, then surely there is something particular that sages and worthies prize in conducting themselves. Try to work this out for me.
Question: Of all things under Heaven, human nature is difficult to discuss. Mengzi lived after Kongzi and distinctively declared that human nature is good. Was this a teaching he had actually received through transmission? “By nature people are close to one another; through habituation they grow apart,” and “The highest in wisdom and the lowest in foolishness do not change” are certainly Kongzi’s words. Might Mengzi’s account, then, conflict with them? Earlier Confucian scholars held that Mengzi’s elucidation of the goodness of human nature was an achievement equal to that of Yu. Had no one before him truly opened the way to this teaching? Master Zhang advanced the statement, “Only after there is bodily form is there a nature constituted by psychophysical endowment,” and Master Zhu followed him. Since then, scholars discussing the study of human nature have all considered that nothing remained to be said. Yet does human nature truly have two forms? Moreover, …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
所謂天命云者果何所指歟孟子而後
究性命之藴莫如周程二子夫二子平
日皆未嘗疑孟氏爲非然而剛柔善惡
之説善惡皆天理之説則又若與相反
者何歟諸生皆誦法孔子者其必有心
得也若夫規規陳言則何以爲深造自
得之學
問嘗聞識時務者在俊傑諸士應賓興而
來人固以俊傑視之已度詞隱義弗以
===
相困姑即爾蜀時務之明且切者相與
共討之夫西南之夷附在職方若松壘
威茂天全芒部永寧諸醜雖世爲邊患
亦既開閫分制而長駕遠馭之道近益
加密爾蜀多士亦既條有成説可采也
乃玆川東諸夷若酉陽石砫平茶邑梅
及播州司屬厥初立之司府官其酋長
蓋與西南若也動爲邊患亦西南若也
建閫設鎮宜無異者乃僅隷之一衛是
punctuated:
所謂天命云者，果何所指歟？孟子而後，究性命之藴，莫如周程二子。夫二子平日皆未嘗疑孟氏爲非，然而剛柔善惡之説、善惡皆天理之説，則又若與相反者，何歟？諸生皆誦法孔子者，其必有心得也。若夫規規陳言，則何以爲深造自得之學？
問：嘗聞識時務者在俊傑。諸士應賓興而來，人固以俊傑視之已。度詞隱義，弗以相困，姑即爾蜀時務之明且切者，相與共討之。夫西南之夷，附在職方，若松壘、威茂、天全、芒部、永寧諸醜，雖世爲邊患，亦既開閫分制，而長駕遠馭之道，近益加密。爾蜀多士，亦既條有成説可采也。乃玆川東諸夷，若酉陽、石砫、平茶、邑梅及播州司屬，厥初立之司府，官其酋長，蓋與西南若也；動爲邊患，亦西南若也。建閫設鎮，宜無異者，乃僅隷之一衛，是
translation_en:
…what, precisely, does the expression “Heaven’s mandate” refer to? After Mengzi, none surpassed the two masters Zhou and Cheng in probing the profundities of human nature and Heaven’s mandate. Neither master ever ordinarily doubted Mengzi’s correctness. Yet their explanations of firmness and yielding, goodness and evil, and the assertion that goodness and evil are both Heaven’s principle seem to contradict him. Why is this? You students all recite Confucius’s teachings and take him as your model; surely you have gained insights of your own. If you merely confine yourselves to received formulations, how can this constitute learning that probes deeply and attains understanding for oneself?
Question: I have heard that those who understand the affairs of their times are men of outstanding ability. You gentlemen have come in response to the summons for the selection and recommendation of worthy men, and people assuredly regard you as men of outstanding ability. We shall not trouble you with obscure wording and hidden meanings [?]; let us instead discuss together those current affairs of your own Shu that are evident and pressing. The non-Han peoples of the southwest are included within the realm’s territorial administration. Such groups as those of Songlei, Weimao, Tianquan, Mangbu, and Yongning have caused trouble on the frontier for generations, but military commands have already been established to control them separately, and methods of exerting authority over these distant regions have recently become still more thorough. You many scholars of Shu have also already set out considered proposals worthy of adoption. Now, the non-Han peoples of eastern Sichuan—such as those of Youyang, Shizhu, Pingcha, Yimei, and the territories subordinate to the Bozhou office—were originally organized into offices and prefectures, with their chieftains appointed as officials, much as in the southwest. They likewise repeatedly cause frontier disturbances, just as in the southwest. There should therefore be no difference in the establishment of military commands and garrisons; yet they have merely been placed under a single guard. Is this …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
果地勢夷情爲足易制邪抑別有說邪
然酉陽石硅切近湖省谿峒諸夷播州
邑平連絡貴竹凱里兵連禍結無歲無
之徒以隔省遥制聲教難及羈縻亦且
虛名事勢蓋甚有難爲處者議者欲於
施州衛
奏設將臣一員專制川湖兩界夷情及議將
川東分巡駐劄重慶者
奏帶兵備請以
===
璽書從事兼制播凱真通變至計也其與控制
西南諸夷事體將無同邪語曰內治脩
而後遠人服信斯言也則內治當脩孰
爲先著遠人未服孰爲後圖邪昔李德
裕節制西川籌邊有樓張詠治成都活
民多術皆內脩外攘之要道二公行之
各有成效可併舉而施之今日否邪請
盡言爲爾鄉謀之毋曰是謀非吾能及
punctuated: 果地勢夷情爲足易制邪？抑別有說邪？然酉陽、石硅切近湖省谿峒諸夷，播州、邑平連絡貴竹、凱里，兵連禍結，無歲無之。徒以隔省遥制，聲教難及，羈縻亦且虛名，事勢蓋甚有難爲處者。議者欲於施州衛奏設將臣一員，專制川湖兩界夷情；及議將川東分巡駐劄重慶者，奏帶兵備，請以璽書從事，兼制播凱，真通變至計也。其與控制西南諸夷，事體將無同邪？語曰：「內治脩而後遠人服。」信斯言也，則內治當脩，孰爲先著？遠人未服，孰爲後圖邪？昔李德裕節制西川，籌邊有樓；張詠治成都，活民多術，皆內脩外攘之要道。二公行之，各有成效，可併舉而施之今日否邪？請盡言，爲爾鄉謀之，毋曰是謀非吾能及。
translation_en:
…is it indeed because the terrain and the circumstances of the non-Han peoples make them easy enough to control? Or is there some other explanation? Yet Youyang and Shigui [石硅, probably Shizhu 石砫; ?] lie very close to the non-Han peoples of the valleys and grottoes of Huguang Province, while Bozhou and Yi-Ping [apparently Yimei and Pingcha; ?] connect with Guizhu and Kaili. Warfare continues and calamities compound one another; no year passes without them. Simply because control is exercised from afar across provincial boundaries, the court’s authority and civilizing influence can scarcely reach them, and even loose-rein administration becomes an empty name. These circumstances indeed present serious difficulties.

Some propose memorializing the throne to establish one military commander at Shizhou Guard, with exclusive responsibility for controlling the non-Han peoples along the Sichuan–Huguang border. They also propose requesting that the surveillance circuit intendant for eastern Sichuan, stationed at Chongqing, concurrently assume responsibility for military preparedness, and that he be empowered by an imperially sealed edict to act, extending his control to Bozhou and Kaili. This is truly an excellent plan for adapting to changing circumstances. Would not the administrative considerations be the same as those involved in controlling the non-Han peoples of the southwest?

As the saying goes, “Only after internal government is put in order do distant peoples submit.” If these words are true, what should be the first measure in putting internal government in order? Since distant peoples have not yet submitted, what should be planned next? Formerly, when Li Deyu exercised military command over Xichuan, he had a tower for planning frontier affairs; when Zhang Yong governed Chengdu, he employed many methods to sustain the people’s lives. These were all essential means of improving government within and repelling threats from without. Both men achieved results through their actions. Could their measures be adopted together and applied today? Please explain your views fully and devise plans for your native province. Do not say that such planning lies beyond your abilities.

translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Qu Boyu sent a messenger to Confucius. Confucius sat with him and asked, “What is your master doing?” He replied, “My master wishes to lessen his faults but has not yet succeeded.” When the messenger had left, the Master said, “What a messenger! What a messenger!”

Fan Xizheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Yao, Instructor: “The literary conception is refined and profound, and the writing elegant and correct. Read closely, the exemplary messenger’s enduring influence and the inner concerns of the worthy of old appear vividly before us in Confucius’s courtyard. Admirable and worthy of emulation.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Shi, Instructor: “The exposition of the passage and the concluding interpretation both contain inexhaustible meaning.” “Beyond the reach of other compositions.”

Comment by Examiner Shi, School Instructor: “Composed and ample, classical and well ordered.”

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “Clear and fluent.”

The sage esteemed the grandee’s messenger and praised his ability to express his master’s worthiness. To do good while feeling that one has not done enough is possible only for someone who has truly attained understanding. Since the messenger could recognize and articulate this, how could he not deserve praise? Formerly, after Confucius had lived in Wei and returned to Lu, Qu Boyu sent a messenger to him, simply to convey his feelings. The Master sat with the messenger and asked what his master was doing, simply to express his affection. title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
聖之懷欲鮮夫率履之咎而湛一之體恒歉於
庸行之常黜乎非而動以善固其一念之拳拳
不忘者雜之欲而間以人其如有萌焉何哉是
雖未能盡如其心而終日乾乾之誠固未敢以
或息矣於是夫了俟其出也從而美之曰使乎
使乎蓋欲彰其主者多溢美之詞不考其素者
非由衷之論使者寡過之云詞謙而益光也未
能之對深思有餘味也雖不必親見其人而與
年俱化之妙固弗能以自掩矣記者於此雖以
===
彰使者而表伯玉而夫子樂善之休擇交之慎
咸見之矣抑嘗因寡過未能之言而論之吉人
爲善惟日不足凶人爲不善亦惟日不足爲善
爲不善猶未甚也至於惟日不足焉則善惡日
長而不可繼矣是故望道未見文王之所以聖
也孳孳爲利跖之所以盜也伯玉五十而知非
六十而化其慕文王而興者乎古者諸侯大夫
旣貴而老猶不廢學躬行之治可久可大有以
也考古而思先王之教可以觀世變矣
punctuated:
聖之懷，欲鮮夫率履之咎，而湛一之體恒歉於庸行之常。黜乎非而動以善，固其一念之拳拳不忘者；雜之欲而間以人，其如有萌焉何哉？是雖未能盡如其心，而終日乾乾之誠，固未敢以或息矣。於是夫了俟其出也，從而美之曰：「使乎！使乎！」蓋欲彰其主者，多溢美之詞；不考其素者，非由衷之論。使者寡過之云，詞謙而益光也；未能之對，深思有餘味也。雖不必親見其人，而與年俱化之妙，固弗能以自掩矣。記者於此，雖以彰使者而表伯玉，而夫子樂善之休、擇交之慎，咸見之矣。

抑嘗因寡過未能之言而論之：吉人爲善，惟日不足；凶人爲不善，亦惟日不足。爲善爲不善，猶未甚也；至於惟日不足焉，則善惡日長而不可繼矣。是故望道未見，文王之所以聖也；孳孳爲利，跖之所以盜也。伯玉五十而知非，六十而化，其慕文王而興者乎？古者諸侯大夫，旣貴而老，猶不廢學，躬行之治可久可大，有以也。考古而思先王之教，可以觀世變矣。
translation_en:
…in his aspiration to sagehood, he wishes to lessen the faults in his conduct, yet, measured against his pure and undivided inner substance, his everyday actions constantly fall short. To reject what is wrong and act according to goodness is surely the single purpose he earnestly keeps in mind and never forgets. But what if selfish desires mingle with it and human impulses intrude, beginning to stir within him? Although he has not yet fully realized his intentions, he has never dared allow his sincere, unremitting effort throughout the day to cease. Thereupon the Master [?; transcribed as 夫了] waited until the messenger had left, then praised him, saying: “What a messenger! What a messenger!” Those who wish to exalt their masters commonly indulge in excessive praise; judgments made without examining a person's habitual conduct do not come from the heart. The messenger's statement about reducing faults was modest in wording but made his master's virtue shine all the more. His reply that his master had not yet succeeded showed deep reflection and left much to ponder. Even without seeing the man himself, one could perceive the subtle transformation that accompanied his advancing years: it could not remain concealed. Although the recorder here commends the messenger and honors Boyu, the Master's admirable delight in goodness and his care in choosing friends are also fully evident.

Moreover, I have considered the words about reducing faults and not yet succeeding. Good people do good as though the days were never sufficient; evil people likewise do evil as though the days were never sufficient. Simply doing good or evil is not yet the utmost point. Once people feel that the days are never sufficient, however, goodness or evil grows daily until it cannot be continued [?]. Thus, looking toward the Way as though he had not yet seen it was what made King Wen a sage; tirelessly pursuing profit was what made Zhi a robber. Boyu recognized his errors at fifty and underwent transformation at sixty: was he not one who was stirred to action by admiration for King Wen? In antiquity, the feudal lords and grand masters, though already honored and advanced in years, still did not abandon learning. There was a reason why their cultivation through personal practice could endure and grow great. By examining antiquity and reflecting upon the teachings of the former kings, one may discern the changes in the world.

其次致曲曲能有誠誠則形形則著著則
明明則動動則變變則化唯天下至誠
爲能化
劉元凱

羣
同考試官教諭陳　批〔縝密而不晦中庸義當〕
如此
考試官學正石　批〔是說理文字〕

中庸論求誠之學而要其與至誠同歸也夫求
誠之學致曲其要矣由是不已以至於化寧不
與至誠者同歸乎中庸是章言人道所以示人
以求誠之學也意謂全體所性而功參造化天
下之至誠則然矣下此着其何以進於誠邪蓋
所謂曲者良心有覺善端之未泯也苟由此而
知端可引也推之以會其全偏可究也致之以
充其量則機心忘矣而本貞弗撓湛一存矣而
punctuated:
其次致曲，曲能有誠，誠則形，形則著，著則明，明則動，動則變，變則化，唯天下至誠爲能化。

劉元凱

同考試官教諭林，批〔發明聖學相因處，詳切超〕羣。

中庸論求誠之學，而要其與至誠同歸也。夫求誠之學，致曲其要矣。由是不已，以至於化，寧不與至誠者同歸乎？中庸是章言人道，所以示人以求誠之學也。意謂全體所性，而功參造化，天下之至誠則然矣。下此着，其何以進於誠邪？蓋所謂曲者，良心有覺，善端之未泯也。苟由此而知端可引也，推之以會其全；偏可究也，致之以充其量，則機心忘矣，而本貞弗撓；湛一存矣，而
translation_en:
“Next come those who fully develop particular beginnings of goodness. These particular beginnings can attain sincerity. Sincerity then takes outward form; taking form, it becomes manifest; becoming manifest, it shines forth; shining forth, it moves others; moving others, it effects change; effecting change, it brings transformation. Only the utmost sincerity under Heaven can bring transformation.”

Liu Yuankai

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Its elucidation of how the stages of sagely learning follow upon one another is detailed and exact, surpassing the ordinary.”

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Closely reasoned without being obscure: this is how the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean should be expounded.”

Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: “This is writing that explicates principle.”

Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “Rounded and substantial.”

The Doctrine of the Mean discusses the learning through which sincerity is sought, insisting that it reach the same destination as utmost sincerity. Fully developing particular beginnings of goodness is the essential point of learning to seek sincerity. If one proceeds from this without ceasing, until one brings transformation, how could one fail to reach the same destination as those of utmost sincerity? This chapter of the Doctrine of the Mean speaks of the human Way in order to show people the learning through which sincerity is sought. Its meaning is that those of utmost sincerity under Heaven fully embody their endowed nature, and their achievement participates in the work of creation and transformation. For those below this level [?], how can they advance toward sincerity? What are called ‘particular beginnings’ are stirrings of awareness in the innate moral heart, the beginnings of goodness that have not been extinguished. If, proceeding from these, one recognizes that a beginning can be extended, and expands it to comprehend the whole; that what is partial can be explored to its fullest extent, and develops it to fill its full capacity—then the calculating mind is forgotten, and one's original rectitude remains unshaken; lucid unity is preserved, and…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
攻取莫累曲其不有誠乎夫惟誠也則積中發
外根心之美宣之而斯形夫惟形也則丕顯成
章生色之休驗之而斯著旣著矣赫喧昭維新
之烈煥乎其有光也不其明乎旣明矣觀感起
好德之良沛然莫之禦也不其動乎由是而之
焉格心向化而習俗殊途之趨革弗俟率之而
始同也由是而之焉恊和時雍而無爲篤恭之
化遠弗見其迹之可擬也然是化也豈易言哉
唯天下至誠盛德泯乎聲臭有以極無方無體
===
之神故萬民忘於道化有以妙不識不知之機
是蓋帝治之極而聖人之能事也夫誠之者今
積而至於化焉又何異於至誠也哉夫曲也者
發於吾心之偏者也化也者極乎聖功之全者
也以聖人之全功而一念之偏可以推之故君
子不求化於聖人而求化於吾心也人苟不是
之思而謂聖人爲不可及聖化爲不可致形著
動變之實用微而因仍苟且之近利出則流於
五霸而已矣五伯者無檢心之功者也曰闇然
punctuated: 攻取莫累，曲其不有誠乎？夫惟誠也，則積中發外，根心之美宣之而斯形。夫惟形也，則丕顯成章，生色之休驗之而斯著。旣著矣，赫喧昭維新之烈，煥乎其有光也，不其明乎？旣明矣，觀感起好德之良，沛然莫之禦也，不其動乎？由是而之焉，格心向化，而習俗殊途之趨革，弗俟率之而始同也。由是而之焉，恊和時雍，而無爲篤恭之化遠，弗見其迹之可擬也。然是化也，豈易言哉？唯天下至誠，盛德泯乎聲臭，有以極無方無體之神，故萬民忘於道化，有以妙不識不知之機。是蓋帝治之極，而聖人之能事也。夫誠之者，今積而至於化焉，又何異於至誠也哉？夫曲也者，發於吾心之偏者也；化也者，極乎聖功之全者也。以聖人之全功，而一念之偏可以推之，故君子不求化於聖人，而求化於吾心也。人苟不是之思，而謂聖人爲不可及，聖化爲不可致，形著動變之實用微，而因仍苟且之近利出，則流於五霸而已矣。五伯者，無檢心之功者也。曰「闇然」
translation_en:
…and striving for acquisition imposes no burden. Would not this particular manifestation of goodness possess sincerity? Only through sincerity does what accumulates within issue forth: the beauty rooted in the heart expresses itself and thus takes form. Only through taking form does it become splendidly apparent and richly patterned: the excellence that gives beauty to the countenance is borne out and thus becomes manifest. Once manifest, it shines resplendently, displaying the achievement of daily renewal. Radiant with light, does it not become luminous? Once luminous, it awakens through observation and inspiration the innate love of virtue, surging irresistibly. Does it not then move others? Proceeding from this, it rectifies hearts and turns them toward transformation; the divergent tendencies of customary practice are reformed, attaining unity without waiting to be directed. Proceeding further, harmony and concord prevail, and the transforming influence of effortless action and profound reverence reaches far, leaving no visible traces that could be imitated. Yet can such transformation be spoken of lightly? Only the utmost sincerity in the world, whose abundant virtue leaves neither sound nor scent, can fully realize the spiritual efficacy that has neither fixed direction nor physical form. Thus the myriad people, unaware of the Way’s transforming influence, embody the wondrous workings of acting without conscious knowledge or awareness. This is the pinnacle of imperial rule and the consummate achievement of the sage.

Now, one who strives to become sincere accumulates effort until attaining transformation. How, then, does such a person differ from one possessed of utmost sincerity? A particular manifestation of goodness arises in one aspect of my heart; transformation brings the entirety of sagely achievement to its culmination. Since the complete achievement of the sage can be reached by extending a single, partial stirring of thought, the gentleman seeks transformation in his own heart. If people fail to reflect on this and say that sagehood is beyond reach and sagely transformation unattainable, the practical efficacy of taking form, becoming manifest, moving others, and bringing change will decline, while short-term advantages gained through habitual expediency will emerge. They will then descend to the level of the Five Hegemons, and no further. The Five Hegemons lacked the work of examining and restraining the heart. It says, “Unobtrusive”…

也固所以求化於心也
詩云迨天之未陰雨徹彼桑土綢繆牖户
今此下民或敢侮予孔子曰爲此詩者
其知道乎能治其國家誰敢侮之

大賢引言治道貴未然之防所以勵時君也甚
矣治貴防於未然也識不早力不易矣如國家
何哉此孟子欲人師古訓以免辱也謂夫辱享
而樂安者大人之所易溺識其重而亟反之殆
人主所以自爲社稷計乎故詩有之曰相彼鳥
矣乘時以圖備患之策故陰雨未迨而桑土是
punctuated:
曰敬信。致曲君子，其於立心之始，若是其不苟也，固所以求化於心也。
《詩》云：「迨天之未陰雨，徹彼桑土，綢繆牖户。今此下民，或敢侮予？」孔子曰：「爲此詩者，其知道乎！能治其國家，誰敢侮之？」
