title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
范希正
同考試官教諭史　批〔至仁以天地萬物爲體神而明之存乎其學古帝王憂民之政孰非此心能以是頌〕
皇上之制作可謂觀其深矣篇末乃復終之以至誠無息之說子得非嘗從
事敬一而有得者乎
考試官學正石　批〔議論究極精微似嘗識仁體者〕
考試官教授李　批〔忠懇見於揄揚中僅見此篇〕
知帝王之學而後可與論帝王之心知帝
王之心而後可與論帝王之制作觀帝王
===
之制作而弗得乎帝王之心猶弗觀也欲
知帝王之心而弗究乎帝王之學終無知
也雖然孟子遡堯舜湯文而併數夫見而
知之之臣禹皐伊萊太公望散宜生凡數
人耳孔子大聖人也能以大哉贊唐堯而
不能名其德則夫以草茅章句之儒由
皇上之制作而欲以仰窺
皇上之學之心豈不猶株守一室而妄談天地
punctuated:
范希正

同考試官教諭史批〔至仁以天地萬物爲體，神而明之，存乎其學。古帝王憂民之政，孰非此心？能以是頌〕皇上之制作，可謂觀其深矣。篇末乃復終之以至誠無息之說，子得非嘗從事敬一而有得者乎？

考試官學正石批〔議論究極精微，似嘗識仁體者。〕

考試官教授李批〔忠懇見於揄揚中，僅見此篇。〕

知帝王之學，而後可與論帝王之心；知帝王之心，而後可與論帝王之制作。觀帝王之制作，而弗得乎帝王之心，猶弗觀也。欲知帝王之心，而弗究乎帝王之學，終無知也。雖然，孟子遡堯舜湯文，而併數夫見而知之之臣，禹、皐、伊、萊、太公望、散宜生，凡數人耳。孔子，大聖人也，能以「大哉」贊唐堯，而不能名其德。則夫以草茅章句之儒，由皇上之制作，而欲以仰窺皇上之學之心，豈不猶株守一室而妄談天地
translation_en:
Fan Xizheng

Comment by Associate Examiner Shi 史, Instructor: 〔“Perfect benevolence takes Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as its own body; bringing this to spiritual efficacy and clear understanding depends upon learning. Which of the ancient emperors’ and kings’ measures for caring for the people did not issue from this heart? To use this understanding to praise〕 His Majesty’s institutions and enactments is truly to perceive their depths. You conclude the essay, moreover, with an account of utmost sincerity that never ceases. Have you perhaps devoted yourself to reverent single-mindedness and gained some insight from it?”

Comment by Examiner Shi 石, Instructor: 〔“The argument probes the utmost subtleties; its author seems to have apprehended the substance of benevolence.”〕

Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: 〔“Loyalty and earnestness emerge amid the praise: only in this essay have I seen this.”〕

Only after understanding the learning of emperors and kings can one discuss their hearts; only after understanding their hearts can one discuss their institutions and enactments. To examine their institutions and enactments without apprehending their hearts is as though one had not examined them at all. To seek to understand their hearts without investigating their learning is ultimately to understand nothing. Yet when Mengzi traced the succession back to Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wen, he also enumerated the ministers who knew them through seeing them: Yu, Gao, Yi, Lai [?], Taigong Wang, and San Yisheng—only a handful in all. Confucius was a great sage: he could praise Tang Yao with the words “Great indeed!” yet could not name his virtue. For a scholar from the countryside, versed in textual explication, to seek through His Majesty’s institutions and enactments to glimpse, with reverence, the heart of His Majesty’s learning—is this not like clinging to a single room while presumptuously discoursing on Heaven and Earth …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
四方者哉顧嘗聞康衢擊壤之流莫非當
時草野之氓而猶能歌咏乎聖帝之治愚
也固草野之氓陳編之所習聞爝火之所
竊照每欲效之歌咏而無由也久矣今請
自比於若人輩可乎且夫無逸之訓七月
之詩皆周公爲成王作也其爲訓也先之
以知稼穡之艱難焉次之以三宗文王之
迪哲焉又次之以小民之違怨詛呪焉何
其簡而嚴直而切也其爲詩也本之乎星
日霜露昆蟲草木之變化焉詳之乎蠶績
耕稼及時乘屋之勞苦焉備及乎上下長
少相與忠愛之情焉何其近而遠婉而該
也自有周訓豳詩以來凡二千年于兹矣
恭惟我
皇上當貞元之會亶
上聖之資
天授龍飛夙承大統乃因西苑之開遂啓殿亭
之制命名取義咸出
punctuated:
四方者哉？顧嘗聞康衢擊壤之流，莫非當時草野之氓，而猶能歌咏乎聖帝之治。愚也固草野之氓，陳編之所習聞，爝火之所竊照，每欲效之歌咏而無由也，久矣。今請自比於若人輩，可乎？且夫《無逸》之訓、《七月》之詩，皆周公爲成王作也。其爲訓也，先之以知稼穡之艱難焉，次之以三宗文王之迪哲焉，又次之以小民之違怨詛呪焉。何其簡而嚴，直而切也！其爲詩也，本之乎星日霜露、昆蟲草木之變化焉，詳之乎蠶績耕稼、及時乘屋之勞苦焉，備及乎上下長少相與忠愛之情焉。何其近而遠，婉而該也！自有周訓豳詩以來，凡二千年于兹矣。
恭惟我皇上，當貞元之會，亶上聖之資，天授龍飛，夙承大統。乃因西苑之開，遂啓殿亭之制，命名取義，咸出
translation_en:
…and the four quarters of the world? Yet I have heard that those who sang on the broad thoroughfare and struck the clods were all common people of the countryside in their day, and even they could sing praises of the sage emperor’s government. I, in my ignorance, am certainly also a common man of the countryside. With what I have learned from old writings, and what my tiny torch has privately illuminated, I have long wished to follow their example in singing praises, but have had no opportunity. May I now venture to compare myself to such people?
The admonition Against Idleness (Wu yi) and the poem The Seventh Month (Qi yue) were both composed by the Duke of Zhou for King Cheng. In the admonition, he begins with understanding the hardships of sowing and reaping; next comes the wisdom practiced by the three ancestral kings and King Wen; and then the disobedience, resentment, and curses of the common people. How concise yet stern, how direct yet pressing! In the poem, he takes as his basis the changes in stars and sun, frost and dew, insects and plants. He describes in detail the toil of tending silkworms, spinning, plowing and planting, and climbing onto roofs at the proper season to repair them. He fully encompasses the feelings of loyalty and affection shared between high and low, old and young. How close to everyday life yet far-reaching, how gentle yet comprehensive! Some two thousand years have now passed since these admonitions of Zhou and poems of Bin came into being.
We reverently consider that our Emperor, at the juncture when an old cycle ends and a new one begins, truly possesses the endowments of the highest sage. Invested by Heaven, he rose like a dragon and early succeeded to the great imperial line. With the opening of the Western Park, he thereupon initiated the construction of halls and pavilions. Their names and the meanings embodied in them all issued from…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
淵衷左右元臣賛揚不暇假物象以寓憂勤
因燕遊而親稼穡此其制作豈非高前古
而震後代者哉愚請以嘗讀典謨而若有
見者姑鋪張而揚厲之帝王之學蓋自堯
舜而始啓其源其見於經曰允執厥中也
曰人心道心也曰惟精惟一也何言乎精
也語夫清明湛一之神常定而萬感之幾
微畢照如寶鑑在手而天下之妍媸莫能
遁也何言乎一也語夫常明不息之貞而
===
流行乎日用無窮之變始而不見其合終
而不見其離也夫是之謂堯舜之學是故
其成位乎中而俯仰乎造化也形於上者
其天乎父道著矣形於下者其地乎母道
察矣形於中者靈者其人而蠢者其物乎
同胞吾與之義彰矣一十二萬九千六百
年之闔闢其一元乎堯舜之一息也上下
四方之極其天地之量乎堯舜之郛廓也
天下之呻吟愁慘與夫夷狄禽獸之或乖
punctuated: 淵衷，左右元臣賛揚不暇。假物象以寓憂勤，因燕遊而親稼穡，此其制作，豈非高前古而震後代者哉？愚請以嘗讀典謨而若有見者，姑鋪張而揚厲之。帝王之學，蓋自堯舜而始啓其源。其見於經，曰「允執厥中」也，曰「人心道心」也，曰「惟精惟一」也。何言乎精也？語夫清明湛一之神常定，而萬感之幾微畢照，如寶鑑在手，而天下之妍媸莫能遁也。何言乎一也？語夫常明不息之貞，而流行乎日用無窮之變，始而不見其合，終而不見其離也。夫是之謂堯舜之學。是故其成位乎中，而俯仰乎造化也，形於上者，其天乎？父道著矣。形於下者，其地乎？母道察矣。形於中者，靈者其人，而蠢者其物乎？同胞吾與之義彰矣。一十二萬九千六百年之闔闢，其一元乎？堯舜之一息也。上下四方之極，其天地之量乎？堯舜之郛廓也。天下之呻吟愁慘，與夫夷狄禽獸之或乖
translation_en:
…the depths of His Majesty’s mind; the chief ministers attending him cannot praise them enough. Through the imagery of things he expresses his anxious diligence, and through leisurely excursions he brings himself close to sowing and reaping. Do not these creations of his surpass those of antiquity and astound later ages? I venture to draw upon such insights as I may have gained from reading the Canons and Counsels, and to elaborate and celebrate them.

The learning of emperors and kings first had its source in Yao and Shun. As it appears in the classic, it says, “Sincerely hold fast to the Mean”; it speaks of “the human mind and the mind of the Way”; and it says, “Be discerning; be single-minded.” What is meant by discernment? It means that the spirit, clear, luminous, tranquil, and unified, remains constantly settled, while fully illuminating the subtlest beginnings of its myriad responses. It is like holding a precious mirror in one’s hand: nothing beautiful or ugly in the world can escape it. What is meant by single-mindedness? It means an enduring constancy, ever luminous and unceasing, that flows through the inexhaustible changes of daily life: at the beginning no joining is discernible, and at the end no separation is discernible. This is what is called the learning of Yao and Shun.

Thus, taking their proper position at the center and looking up and down upon the workings of creation, they see what takes form above—is this not Heaven? The way of the father is manifest. What takes form below—is this not Earth? The way of the mother is evident. Among what takes form between them, are not the spiritually perceptive human beings, and those that merely stir the other creatures? The meaning of regarding the people as one’s siblings and other creatures as one’s companions is made plain. The closing and opening of 129,600 years—is this not a single cosmic cycle? It is but one breath of Yao and Shun. The utmost extent above and below and in the four directions—is this not the measure of Heaven and Earth? It is the outer enclosure of Yao and Shun. The groaning, sorrow, and misery throughout the world, together with any deviation by the Yi and Di peoples, birds, and beasts …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
其理其物之不得所乎皆堯舜之疾痛痾
癢痿痺不仁也當時之臣贊之曰帝德廣
運蓋有以識此矣宋儒程顥曰至仁者以
天地爲一身而天地之間品物萬形皆其
四肢百體蓋亦嘗窺堯舜而知之者也夫
是之謂與天地合德夫是之謂堯舜之心
又嘗伏讀我
皇上敬一之箴而竊有覺焉
聖箴曰敬者存其心而不忽之謂也其堯舜之
===
所謂精乎曰一者純其心而不雜之謂也
其堯舜之所謂一乎唐虞代遠精義湮微
何其越千古而合轍也夫我
皇上之學卽堯舜之學則知我
皇上之心卽堯舜之心我
皇上之心卽堯舜之心則凡先天下而爲之憂
者宜固無所不用其極豈待觀古人之詩
書而後能切切爲天下計乎是故覽無逸
而搆殿非得之書也書之精義
punctuated:
其理，其物之不得所乎？皆堯舜之疾痛痾癢、痿痺不仁也。當時之臣贊之曰：「帝德廣運。」蓋有以識此矣。宋儒程顥曰：「至仁者以天地爲一身，而天地之間品物萬形，皆其四肢百體。」蓋亦嘗窺堯舜而知之者也。夫是之謂與天地合德，夫是之謂堯舜之心。
又嘗伏讀我皇上敬一之箴，而竊有覺焉。聖箴曰：「敬者，存其心而不忽之謂也。」其堯舜之所謂精乎？曰：「一者，純其心而不雜之謂也。」其堯舜之所謂一乎？唐虞代遠，精義湮微，何其越千古而合轍也！夫我皇上之學卽堯舜之學，則知我皇上之心卽堯舜之心。我皇上之心卽堯舜之心，則凡先天下而爲之憂者，宜固無所不用其極，豈待觀古人之詩書，而後能切切爲天下計乎？是故覽無逸而搆殿，非得之書也。書之精義……
translation_en:
…their proper principles—are these instances of beings failing to find their proper place? All are felt by Yao and Shun as their own pain and illness, itching, weakness, paralysis, and numbness. Ministers of that time praised the sovereign, saying, “The emperor’s virtue is vast and far-reaching.” Surely they had some understanding of this. The Song Confucian Cheng Hao said, “The person of utmost benevolence regards Heaven and Earth as one body, and the myriad kinds and forms of things between Heaven and Earth as its limbs and bodily parts.” He too had surely glimpsed Yao and Shun and understood them. This is what is meant by matching Heaven and Earth in virtue; this is what is meant by the heart of Yao and Shun.
I have also reverently read Our Emperor’s Admonition on Reverence and Oneness and privately gained an insight. The imperial admonition says, “Reverence means preserving one’s heart and not neglecting it.” Is this not what Yao and Shun called “refinement”? It says, “Oneness means keeping one’s heart pure and unmixed.” Is this not what Yao and Shun called “oneness”? The ages of Tang and Yu are distant, and their subtle teachings have become obscured. How remarkable that, across thousands of years, these teachings should follow the same course! Since Our Emperor’s learning is the learning of Yao and Shun, we know that Our Emperor’s heart is the heart of Yao and Shun. Since Our Emperor’s heart is the heart of Yao and Shun, in all matters of taking thought for the world’s troubles before others do, he must surely exert himself to the utmost. How could he need to wait until he had read the ancients’ Odes and Documents before earnestly planning for the realm? Thus, when he read “Against Idleness” and built a hall, he did not derive his understanding from the Documents. The essential meaning of the Documents…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
聖衷實先得之顧因書而相感耳取豳風而命
亭非得之詩也詩之精義
聖衷實先得之顧因詩而相感耳昔者伏羲嘗
因河圖而畫卦矣世儒孰不以非河圖則
卦無由畫也不知河圖未出伏羲胷中固
先已具有成卦矣神禹嘗因洛書而作範
矣世儒孰不以非洛書則範無由作也不
知洛書未出神禹胷中固先已具有成範
矣是故畏天命悲人窮以是頌
皇上之制作似矣未盡也嘉唐虞樂商周以是
===
頌我
皇上之制作似矣未盡也易曰知崇禮卑崇效
天卑法地我
皇上之知其效諸天乎
淵襟獨契之妙其合德天地而與堯舜同其
廣大乎其由敬一而得之者乎彼宮�youre之
隙秸穗之場𥡴材藻煥堀爾星輝納薫風
而解愠率俊乂以游歌其先天下之憂有
punctuated:
聖衷實先得之，顧因書而相感耳。取豳風而命亭，非得之詩也，詩之精義，聖衷實先得之，顧因詩而相感耳。昔者伏羲嘗因河圖而畫卦矣，世儒孰不以非河圖則卦無由畫也？不知河圖未出，伏羲胷中固先已具有成卦矣。神禹嘗因洛書而作範矣，世儒孰不以非洛書則範無由作也？不知洛書未出，神禹胷中固先已具有成範矣。是故畏天命，悲人窮，以是頌皇上之制作，似矣，未盡也；嘉唐虞，樂商周，以是頌我皇上之制作，似矣，未盡也。
易曰：「知崇禮卑，崇效天，卑法地。」我皇上之知，其效諸天乎？淵襟獨契之妙，其合德天地而與堯舜同其廣大乎？其由敬一而得之者乎？彼宮�youre之隙，秸穗之場，𥡴材藻煥，堀爾星輝，納薫風而解愠，率俊乂以游歌，其先天下之憂有
translation_en:
…Your Majesty’s sagely heart had in fact already grasped it; the Book of Documents merely awakened a sympathetic response. Taking the Airs of Bin as the basis for naming a pavilion likewise did not mean acquiring this understanding from the Book of Odes. Your Majesty’s sagely heart had in fact already grasped the profound meaning of the Odes; the poems merely awakened a sympathetic response. In antiquity, Fuxi drew the trigrams in response to the River Chart. What scholar of later ages does not suppose that without the River Chart there would have been no way to draw the trigrams? They do not realize that, before the River Chart appeared, Fuxi already possessed the completed trigrams within his breast. The divine Yu composed the Great Plan in response to the Luo Writing. What scholar of later ages does not suppose that without the Luo Writing there would have been no way to compose the Great Plan? They do not realize that, before the Luo Writing appeared, the divine Yu already possessed the completed Great Plan within his breast. Thus, to praise Your Majesty’s creations as expressing reverence for Heaven’s mandate and compassion for the people’s distress is fitting, but does not exhaust their meaning. To praise Your Majesty’s creations as expressing admiration for Tang and Yu and delight in Shang and Zhou is fitting, but does not exhaust their meaning.
The Book of Changes says: “Wisdom is lofty; ritual is humble. The lofty emulates Heaven; the humble models itself on Earth.” Does not Your Majesty’s wisdom emulate Heaven? Does the wondrous understanding uniquely attained in Your Majesty’s profound heart unite its virtue with Heaven and Earth and share the vastness of Yao and Shun? Is it attained through reverent concentration on the One? There, in a space within the palace [?], on a ground of stalks and ears of grain, the timber and ornament shine [?], rising with the brilliance of stars. Welcoming the balmy wind to dispel discontent, leading men of outstanding talent to stroll and sing—Your Majesty’s concern, which precedes that of all under Heaven, has…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
不容已因感而發之者乎易又曰聖人以
此洗心退藏於密吉凶與民同患神以知
來知以藏往其孰能與於此哉古之聰明
睿知神武而不殺者夫正我
皇上今日制作之謂矣昔我
皇祖倥偬未暇屢詔勸農爲旱祈天曝晝寢地
追我
成祖親馭六飛掃除殘醜乃命
仁皇周爰巡省此其憂天下之心堯舜何加焉
===
愚又知我
皇上制作之心蓋上繼堯舜而增光
烈祖矣若夫後世人主如漢文帝之屢賜田租
晉武帝之焚裘前殿唐太宗之吞蝗宋仁
宗之觀麥比跡而觀雖與文王之卑服卽
康功田功者不倸然未聞乎堯舜之學則
必無得乎堯舜之心是皆所謂希慕往跡
而爲之者不足道也夫生太平之世親見
大聖人之制作而又服習乎
punctuated:
不容已，因感而發之者乎？《易》又曰：「聖人以此洗心，退藏於密，吉凶與民同患。神以知來，知以藏往，其孰能與於此哉？古之聰明睿知、神武而不殺者夫！」正我皇上今日制作之謂矣。昔我皇祖倥偬未暇，屢詔勸農，爲旱祈天，曝晝寢地。追我成祖親馭六飛，掃除殘醜，乃命仁皇周爰巡省。此其憂天下之心，堯舜何加焉？
愚又知我皇上制作之心，蓋上繼堯舜而增光烈祖矣。若夫後世人主，如漢文帝之屢賜田租、晉武帝之焚裘前殿、唐太宗之吞蝗、宋仁宗之觀麥，比跡而觀，雖與文王之卑服卽康功田功者不倸，然未聞乎堯舜之學，則必無得乎堯舜之心。是皆所謂希慕往跡而爲之者，不足道也。夫生太平之世，親見大聖人之制作，而又服習乎
translation_en:
…could not be restrained, and found expression in response to what moved him? The Book of Changes further says: “By this the sage cleanses his heart and withdraws into secrecy; in good fortune and ill, he shares the people's anxieties. Through spiritual insight he knows what is to come; through wisdom he stores up what has passed. Who could attain to this? Surely those of antiquity who were discerning, clear-sighted, sagacious, and wise, divinely martial yet did not kill!” This describes precisely the works of our present Emperor. In former days, our imperial progenitor, though pressed by affairs and without leisure, repeatedly issued edicts encouraging agriculture. During drought he prayed to Heaven, exposing himself to the daytime sun and sleeping on the ground. Recalling our Chengzu, he personally drove the imperial six-horse chariot to sweep away the remaining villains, then commanded Emperor Renzong to make inspection tours far and wide. How could Yao and Shun have surpassed such concern for all under Heaven?
I further understand that the intention behind our Emperor's works is to carry on the legacy of Yao and Shun and add glory to his illustrious ancestors. As for rulers of later ages—Emperor Wen of Han repeatedly remitting land taxes, Emperor Wu of Jin burning a fur robe before the palace hall, Emperor Taizong of Tang swallowing locusts, and Emperor Renzong of Song inspecting wheat—if we compare their deeds, they were perhaps not unlike [?] King Wen, who wore humble clothing and devoted himself to the work of securing the people's welfare and cultivating the fields. Yet, having never learned the teachings of Yao and Shun, they necessarily failed to grasp the heart of Yao and Shun. These were all instances of what is called acting out of admiration for the deeds of the past, and are not worth discussing. Now, born into an age of great peace, personally witnessing the works of a great sage, and moreover diligently studying…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
皇極敷言之訓苟不能效一詞焉以從乎見知
諸臣之後寧不爲負生成而自棄於天地
者耶子思子曰至誠無息不息則久久則
徵徵則悠遠悠遠則愽厚愽厚則高明愽
厚配地高明配天悠久無疆愚請以是爲
今日獻
第二問
梅友竹
同考試官教諭史　批〔異同之評通變之術皆根〕
===
〔据要實且筆勢翩翩不艱深險澁吾將自慶得子於驪黃〕
〔之外矣〕
考試官學正石　批〔知言知心此策近之〕
考試官教授李　批〔不泛不略〕
明聖人之道者救天下之時者也守先王
之法者保天下之治者也夫聖賢事君之
心一也而其敷言以告君者則各有所之
而不能以一之也於其不能一之者之中
而要其歸焉而未始有或異者是故因之
punctuated:
皇極敷言之訓，苟不能效一詞焉，以從乎見知諸臣之後，寧不爲負生成而自棄於天地者耶？子思子曰：「至誠無息，不息則久，久則徵，徵則悠遠，悠遠則愽厚，愽厚則高明。愽厚配地，高明配天，悠久無疆。」愚請以是爲今日獻。
第二問
梅友竹
同考試官教諭史批〔異同之評、通變之術，皆根据要實，且筆勢翩翩，不艱深險澁，吾將自慶得子於驪黃之外矣。〕
考試官學正石批〔知言知心，此策近之。〕
考試官教授李批〔不泛不略。〕
明聖人之道者，救天下之時者也；守先王之法者，保天下之治者也。夫聖賢事君之心一也，而其敷言以告君者，則各有所之，而不能以一之也。於其不能一之者之中，而要其歸焉，而未始有或異者。是故因之
translation_en:
…the instruction concerning the sovereign’s pronouncements on the August Standard. If I cannot offer even a single statement, following behind the ministers who understand the sage through having witnessed him, would I not betray the grace that has nurtured me and cast myself out from Heaven and Earth? Master Zisi said: “Utmost sincerity never ceases. Never ceasing, it endures; enduring, it becomes manifest; becoming manifest, it extends far; extending far, it becomes broad and substantial; becoming broad and substantial, it becomes lofty and luminous. In breadth and substance it matches Earth; in loftiness and luminosity it matches Heaven. Its enduring reach has no bounds.” I humbly ask to offer these words today.
Second Question
Mei Youzhu
Comment by Associate Examiner Shi 史, Instructor: “His assessment of similarities and differences and his methods of adapting to change are all grounded in essentials and practical realities. Moreover, his writing flows gracefully, without obscurity or awkwardness. I shall congratulate myself on having found you by looking beyond outward appearances, as a judge of horses looks beyond whether they are black or yellow.”
Comment by Examiner Shi 石, School Instructor: “Understanding words and understanding the mind: this policy essay comes close to both.”
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: “Neither vague nor cursory.”
Those who elucidate the Way of the sages remedy the troubles of their age throughout the realm; those who uphold the laws of the former kings preserve order throughout the realm. The sages and worthies share one intention in serving their rulers, yet the statements they set forth to advise them each have a particular aim and cannot be made uniform. Amid these statements that cannot be made uniform, if one seeks their ultimate purpose, there has never been any difference. Thus, what they follow …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
者機也而應之者順也聖賢何容心哉執
事以孟子告君之言與伊傅周孔不同下
詢承學愚不敏何足以知之請即其所以
異而要其所以同者以復明問可乎且孟
子之時何時邪天下無王矣邪說横行矣
以功利爲心以攻伐爲賢滔滔皆是矣一
旦見齊王因其足用爲善凡所以告之者
非堯舜之道則不敢陳焉今具載七篇之
中炳炳如丹可考也且夫堯舜之道何道
===
也仁之至也義之盡也苟欲正人心息邪
說以行王道以平治天下者舍此奚以哉
此孟子汲汲皇皇以之救時者用心亦良
苦矣乃若伊尹傅說周公孔子之時天下
一統也故其告君拳拳以法祖爲言如曰
烈祖之成德如曰先王之成憲如曰儀刑
文王如曰文武之政諄諄告戒不一而足
蓋以祖宗之法爲子孫者皆當世守之以
保治而不可作聰明以亂之也其不以堯
punctuated: 者，機也；而應之者，順也。聖賢何容心哉？執事以孟子告君之言與伊傅周孔不同，下詢承學。愚不敏，何足以知之？請即其所以異，而要其所以同者，以復明問，可乎？且孟子之時何時邪？天下無王矣，邪說横行矣，以功利爲心，以攻伐爲賢，滔滔皆是矣。一旦見齊王，因其足用爲善，凡所以告之者，非堯舜之道則不敢陳焉。今具載七篇之中，炳炳如丹，可考也。且夫堯舜之道，何道也？仁之至也，義之盡也。苟欲正人心、息邪說，以行王道，以平治天下者，舍此奚以哉？此孟子汲汲皇皇以之救時者，用心亦良苦矣。乃若伊尹、傅說、周公、孔子之時，天下一統也，故其告君，拳拳以法祖爲言。如曰「烈祖之成德」，如曰「先王之成憲」，如曰「儀刑文王」，如曰「文武之政」，諄諄告戒，不一而足。蓋以祖宗之法，爲子孫者皆當世守之，以保治，而不可作聰明以亂之也。其不以堯
translation_en:
…was the exigency of the moment; their response accorded with it. How could sages and worthies impose any private intention? You, sir, observing that Mengzi’s words to rulers differed from those of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Kongzi, have condescended to question us students. Dull-witted as I am, how could I adequately understand this? May I examine wherein they differed and identify wherein they agreed, in reply to your discerning question?

What sort of age was Mengzi’s? All under Heaven lacked a true king; heterodox teachings ran rampant. Those who set their hearts on achievement and profit and deemed military conquest worthy were everywhere, like a surging flood. When he came to meet the king of Qi, recognizing his capacity to do good, he dared present nothing to him that was not the Way of Yao and Shun. His words are now fully recorded in the seven books of the Mengzi, as brilliantly clear as cinnabar, and may be consulted. And what is the Way of Yao and Shun? It is benevolence brought to its utmost and righteousness fully realized. If one wishes to rectify people’s hearts, put an end to heterodox teachings, practice the Kingly Way, and bring peace and order to all under Heaven, what could one use apart from this? Mengzi urgently and anxiously employed it to rescue his age; his efforts were indeed painstaking.

As for the times of Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Kongzi, all under Heaven was united. Thus, in addressing their rulers, they earnestly spoke of taking the ancestors as models. Such statements as “the accomplished virtue of the illustrious ancestor,” “the established statutes of the former kings,” “take King Wen as your model,” and “the government of Kings Wen and Wu” offered repeated, earnest admonitions too numerous to enumerate. For the laws of the ancestors were to be preserved from generation to generation by all their descendants, so as to maintain good order; they must not disrupt them by displaying their own cleverness. That they did not speak of Yao …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
舜爲言者蓋以成湯文武立法之善經緯
乎一心會通乎萬化仁至義盡皆祖述堯
舜之道而爲之者故法乎祖者即法乎堯
舜也中間因革損益與世推移而不能以
强同之者勢也而其大公至正上下與天
地同流之心先聖後聖揆之何嘗有不一
邪而孟子不告齊王以法祖者彼齊之先
世垂裕未嘗無法不過霸政之遺烈而已
以之撥亂反正而一天下未見其可也夫
===
何言哉卽此而觀使孟子當商周一統之
時其告君保治必以法祖爲言而不言堯
舜矣使伊傅周孔當戰國糜爛之際其告
君救時必以堯舜爲言而不言法祖矣誰
謂聖賢易地而不皆然邪第伊傅周公幸
遇其君而道行焉孔孟雖不幸不遇於當
時而師表百王與天無極庸非萬世之幸
與抑愚於此竊有說焉道者所以立本也
不容或異法者所以適變也不必盡同凡
punctuated:
舜爲言者，蓋以成湯文武立法之善，經緯乎一心，會通乎萬化，仁至義盡，皆祖述堯舜之道而爲之者。故法乎祖者，即法乎堯舜也。中間因革損益，與世推移，而不能以强同之者，勢也。而其大公至正、上下與天地同流之心，先聖後聖揆之，何嘗有不一邪？而孟子不告齊王以法祖者，彼齊之先世垂裕，未嘗無法，不過霸政之遺烈而已。以之撥亂反正而一天下，未見其可也。夫何言哉？卽此而觀，使孟子當商周一統之時，其告君保治，必以法祖爲言，而不言堯舜矣。使伊傅周孔當戰國糜爛之際，其告君救時，必以堯舜爲言，而不言法祖矣。誰謂聖賢易地而不皆然邪？第伊傅周公幸遇其君而道行焉，孔孟雖不幸不遇於當時，而師表百王，與天無極，庸非萬世之幸與？
抑愚於此竊有說焉：道者，所以立本也，不容或異；法者，所以適變也，不必盡同。凡
translation_en:
…Shun as their subject, because the excellence of the institutions established by Cheng Tang and Kings Wen and Wu was ordered within a single mind and comprehensively adapted to the myriad transformations. Consummate in benevolence and exhaustive in righteousness, these institutions were all made by following and carrying forward the Way of Yao and Shun. Thus, taking one’s ancestors as models is precisely to take Yao and Shun as models. That, in the course of this, institutions were retained or reformed, reduced or augmented, changing with the times and incapable of being forced into uniformity, was a matter of circumstances. Yet their utterly impartial and supremely upright hearts, moving together with Heaven and Earth above and below—when the earlier and later sages are measured against this standard, when have they ever differed?
Mengzi did not tell the King of Qi to model himself on his ancestors because, although Qi’s forebears had certainly left institutions to benefit their descendants, these were merely the surviving achievements of hegemonic rule. It was not apparent how they could be used to quell disorder, restore proper order, and unite all under Heaven. What, then, could he say of them? Viewed in this light, had Mengzi lived during the unified rule of Shang or Zhou, in advising his ruler on preserving good government he would surely have spoken of following the ancestors, rather than of Yao and Shun. Had Yi Yin, Fu Yue, the Duke of Zhou, and Kongzi lived amid the devastation of the Warring States, in advising their rulers on remedying the troubles of the age they would surely have spoken of Yao and Shun, rather than of following the ancestors. Who could say that sages and worthies, exchanging places, would not all have acted thus? It was simply that Yi Yin, Fu Yue, and the Duke of Zhou were fortunate enough to meet rulers who recognized them, so that their Way was put into practice. Although Kongzi and Mengzi were unfortunate in finding no such recognition in their own time, they became teachers and exemplars for a hundred generations of kings, enduring without limit alongside Heaven. Was this not a blessing for all ages?
Yet I, in my humble view, venture to offer a further observation here: the Way is that by which the foundation is established, and it admits of no divergence; institutions are that by which one accommodates change, and they need not all be identical. As for all…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
祖法之善者雖百世由之可也然世變無
窮亦有不容不少變者要當本之以大公
至正之心權其宜而通其變其始也必議
之公而不偏其終也必守之固而不搖如
漢文帝除挾書之禁除誹謗之令除肉刑
之慘雖紛更乎高帝之約束而革故鼎新
深仁厚澤於漢德有光焉君子又烏可拘
於世守無愆而爲執一之論哉管窺如斯
惟執事進而敎之
===
第三問
金深
同考試官教諭陳 批〔漢晉士風過中失正正坐殉〕
時而不能殉道之弊子能摘取以爲斷案似又過宋
儒言論之表且評品精確使諸賢復生亦當首肯矣
他日立
朝慎毋負斯言哉
考試官學正石 批〔議論抑揚開闔有廉頑立〕
懦之風足以占子之槩已
punctuated:
祖法之善者，雖百世由之可也。然世變無窮，亦有不容不少變者。要當本之以大公至正之心，權其宜而通其變。其始也，必議之公而不偏；其終也，必守之固而不搖。如漢文帝除挾書之禁，除誹謗之令，除肉刑之慘，雖紛更乎高帝之約束，而革故鼎新，深仁厚澤，於漢德有光焉。君子又烏可拘於世守無愆，而爲執一之論哉？管窺如斯，惟執事進而敎之。

第三問
金深

同考試官教諭陳批〔漢晉士風過中失正，正坐殉〕時而不能殉道之弊。子能摘取以爲斷案，似又過宋儒言論之表。且評品精確，使諸賢復生，亦當首肯矣。他日立朝，慎毋負斯言哉！

考試官學正石批〔議論抑揚開闔，有廉頑立〕懦之風，足以占子之槩已。
translation_en:
…those ancestral laws that are good may be followed even for a hundred generations. Yet changes in the world are inexhaustible, and some things cannot but undergo a measure of alteration. What matters is to take as one’s foundation a mind of utmost impartiality and rectitude, weigh what is appropriate, and adapt to changing circumstances. At the outset, deliberations must be impartial and free from bias; afterward, the resulting measures must be upheld firmly and without wavering. For example, Emperor Wen of the Han abolished the prohibition on possessing books, repealed the ordinance against criticism, and eliminated the cruelty of mutilating punishments. Although these measures altered the regulations of Emperor Gao, they removed the old and established the new; their profound benevolence and abundant beneficence brought lustre to Han virtue. How, then, could a gentleman be constrained by the injunction to preserve inherited institutions without error and argue for rigid adherence to a single course? Such is my narrow view. I ask you, sir, to guide and instruct me further.

Third Question
Jin Shen 金深

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: The ethos of scholars under the Han and Jin went beyond the mean and lost its proper balance, precisely because of the failing of devoting themselves to the times rather than to the Way. You have singled this out as the basis for a definitive judgment, seemingly going even beyond the pronouncements of the Song Confucians. Moreover, your assessments are precise: were those worthies to return to life, they too would surely nod in assent. When you one day take your place at court, take care not to betray these words!

Comment by Examiner Shi, School Instructor: Your argument, in its censure and praise, its development and resolution, has the power to make the avaricious upright and the timid resolute. It is enough to reveal the tenor of your character.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
考試官教授李　批　評論古人往迹莫逃鑒別
有學有守士也録之
君子中立於天下也當以道殉身而不以
身殉時道也者君子所殉以生之理也隨
時而用中君子所以善夫道也使或過焉
則失之矯亢或不及焉則淪于卑汙皆非
道之本體然也孟子曰天下有道以道殉
身天下無道以身殉道蓋言道可殉而時
不可殉也執是以論漢晉之士風正坐殉
===
時而不能殉道之弊自今觀之或去道之
遠或竊夫道之近似人品志行雖高下清
濁之不同律以中行之道則槩乎未之有
聞也執事以是下詢承學則所以挽頽波
喚大寐以植立當世之士風意亦獨至矣
愚也敢不上承嘉惠忍負平生以孤我
清朝作養之盛典乎慨自高帝不好儒術一
時頑鈍無恥者望風歸之間有號爲儒者
亦不過以佔畢訓詁爲事上不能推尋學
punctuated:
考試官教授李批：評論古人往迹，莫逃鑒別。有學有守士也，録之。

君子中立於天下也，當以道殉身，而不以身殉時。道也者，君子所殉以生之理也。隨時而用中，君子所以善夫道也。使或過焉，則失之矯亢；或不及焉，則淪于卑汙，皆非道之本體然也。孟子曰：「天下有道，以道殉身；天下無道，以身殉道。」蓋言道可殉，而時不可殉也。執是以論漢晉之士風，正坐殉時而不能殉道之弊。自今觀之，或去道之遠，或竊夫道之近似，人品志行雖高下清濁之不同，律以中行之道，則槩乎未之有聞也。執事以是下詢承學，則所以挽頽波、喚大寐，以植立當世之士風，意亦獨至矣。愚也敢不上承嘉惠，忍負平生，以孤我清朝作養之盛典乎？慨自高帝不好儒術，一時頑鈍無恥者望風歸之，間有號爲儒者，亦不過以佔畢訓詁爲事，上不能推尋學
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Li, Professor: In his assessment of the deeds of the ancients, nothing escapes his discerning judgment. He is a scholar of learning and firm principles. Admit him.

The gentleman maintains a balanced position in the world: he should have the Way attend upon his person, rather than sacrifice his person to the times. The Way is the principle that the gentleman follows in living. To act according to the mean as circumstances change is how the gentleman rightly practices the Way. If he goes too far, he errs through affected loftiness; if he falls short, he sinks into baseness and impurity. Neither accords with the essential nature of the Way. Mencius said: “When the world possesses the Way, have the Way attend upon one's person; when the world lacks the Way, sacrifice one's person for the Way.” This means that one may sacrifice oneself for the Way, but not for the times. Judged by this principle, the ethos of scholars under the Han and Jin suffered precisely from sacrificing themselves to the times while failing to sacrifice themselves for the Way. Viewed from the present, some strayed far from the Way, while others appropriated its semblance. Although their character, aspirations, and conduct differed in elevation and baseness, purity and impurity, measured against the Way of balanced conduct, scarcely any can be said to have exemplified it.

By condescending to question us students on this matter, you seek to turn back the tide of decline and awaken those sunk in deep slumber, thereby establishing the ethos of scholars in the present age. Your intention is most profound. Dull as I am, dare I fail to receive your gracious favor? Could I bear to betray my lifelong commitments and disappoint our illustrious dynasty's magnificent undertaking of nurturing talent?

It is lamentable that, since Emperor Gao had no liking for Confucian learning, the obtuse and shameless men of his time flocked to him as soon as they perceived his inclinations. Among them, those who were called Confucians did no more than occupy themselves with reciting texts and explaining words. At the higher level, they could not trace learning …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
問之源流次又不能以名節自立於衰世
蓋自董相申公數人之外無復儒者氣象
曲學者阿世講禮者貪鄙明經者志于青
紫士習卑陋波蕩風流宜乎王莽篡竊之
日貢符獻瑞一朝成羣也光武力矯斯弊
物色嚴光崇尚名節以變其風而中世以
來英傑挺生清議相尚雖視昔儒有愧然
守義不變有足尚焉者迨漢末造國勢不
絕如綫奸雄染指漢鼎而猶畏夫名義未
敢公然即取者諸君子維持之力未可誣
也宋儒呂伯恭乃謂東漢尚節義不若西
漢蓋激于實有名亡而言未可執一以例
夫天下之通論也清議之尚所以端士習
扶人紀國家賴之公論所由出也而東漢
諸賢乃品題標異處已過高搏擊豪强嫉
惡太甚圖艱撥亂之際而又亟失事機之
會激爲黨禍延及善類凡以自處之道有
未盡耳夫豈清議之咎南軒張敬夫謂其
punctuated:
問之源流，次又不能以名節自立於衰世。蓋自董相、申公數人之外，無復儒者氣象。曲學者阿世，講禮者貪鄙，明經者志于青紫。士習卑陋，波蕩風流，宜乎王莽篡竊之日，貢符獻瑞，一朝成羣也。光武力矯斯弊，物色嚴光，崇尚名節以變其風。而中世以來，英傑挺生，清議相尚，雖視昔儒有愧，然守義不變，有足尚焉者。迨漢末造，國勢不絕如綫，奸雄染指漢鼎，而猶畏夫名義，未敢公然即取者，諸君子維持之力未可誣也。宋儒呂伯恭乃謂東漢尚節義不若西漢，蓋激于實有名亡而言，未可執一以例夫天下之通論也。

清議之尚，所以端士習、扶人紀，國家賴之，公論所由出也。而東漢諸賢乃品題標異，處已過高，搏擊豪强，嫉惡太甚。圖艱撥亂之際，而又亟失事機之會，激爲黨禍，延及善類，凡以自處之道有未盡耳，夫豈清議之咎？南軒張敬夫謂其
translation_en:
…the origins and development of learning; nor, at the next level, could they establish themselves through reputation and integrity in an age of decline. Apart from Minister Dong, Master Shen, and a few others, none retained the bearing of a Confucian scholar. Those who distorted learning pandered to their age; those who expounded ritual were greedy and base; those versed in the Classics aspired to the blue and purple insignia of high office. Scholars’ habits were mean and vulgar, and their influence spread like surging waves. Little wonder that, when Wang Mang usurped the throne, those presenting auspicious tokens and portents gathered in crowds overnight. Guangwu vigorously corrected these abuses. He sought out Yan Guang and exalted reputation and integrity to transform prevailing customs. From the middle of the dynasty onward, outstanding men emerged, esteeming one another through principled public judgment. Although they fell short of the Confucians of antiquity, their unwavering adherence to righteousness deserved esteem. By the final years of the Han, the dynasty’s survival hung by a thread. Ambitious villains coveted the Han’s sovereign power, yet still feared the claims of legitimacy and righteousness and dared not openly seize it at once. The contribution of these gentlemen to sustaining the dynasty cannot be denied. Yet the Song Confucian Lü Bogong maintained that the Eastern Han’s esteem for integrity and righteousness did not equal that of the Western Han. His statement was presumably provoked by the circumstance that substance existed while reputation was absent [?]; this one assertion cannot be made the standard for a comprehensive judgment of the matter.

Esteem for principled public judgment serves to rectify scholars’ habits and uphold the ethical bonds of human society. The state depends upon it, and impartial public opinion arises from it. Yet the worthy men of the Eastern Han ranked people and singled them out for distinction, set themselves too high, assailed the powerful, and carried their hatred of evil too far. When confronting difficulties and restoring order, they repeatedly missed opportunities for effective action. They thereby provoked the partisan persecutions, which spread to other good men. All this arose simply because their way of conducting themselves was not fully adequate. How could principled public judgment itself be to blame? Nanxuan, Zhang Jingfu, said that they…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
失處困亨屯之道者此也南軒又謂名節
之稱起于衰世葢以昔儒學問素充隨時
形著不嶄立節而節不可奪不嶄殉名而
名自隨之至於世衰道微能有自拔于流
俗卓立于衰世者世以名節歸之而士君
子道學未至亦以此自負耳非謂盛世不
貴乎名節也昔司馬光悲黨人生昏亂之
世不能避小人之禍深有取於郭泰申屠
蟠者葢一則不爲危言激論處濁世而怨
===
禍不及一則見幾而作超然免于評論明
哲保身之道固當爾也至南軒追論其事
乃以李膺杜密陳蕃入於仲由之科以陳
寔郭泰黄憲入于顔氏之科非無謂也葢
李膺杜密陳蕃輩所行雖正立節雖嚴未
免發于意氣所動而非由於義理之安出
於惡其聲之所感而未盡夫惻隱之實使
在聖門作而成之可與仲由竝駕也陳太
丘持心最平而所處張讓之事亦未中節
punctuated: 失處困亨屯之道者，此也。南軒又謂名節之稱起于衰世，葢以昔儒學問素充，隨時形著，不嶄立節而節不可奪，不嶄殉名而名自隨之。至於世衰道微，能有自拔于流俗、卓立于衰世者，世以名節歸之，而士君子道學未至，亦以此自負耳，非謂盛世不貴乎名節也。昔司馬光悲黨人生昏亂之世，不能避小人之禍，深有取於郭泰、申屠蟠者，葢一則不爲危言激論，處濁世而怨禍不及；一則見幾而作，超然免于評論。明哲保身之道，固當爾也。至南軒追論其事，乃以李膺、杜密、陳蕃入於仲由之科，以陳寔、郭泰、黄憲入于顔氏之科，非無謂也。葢李膺、杜密、陳蕃輩所行雖正，立節雖嚴，未免發于意氣所動，而非由於義理之安，出於惡其聲之所感，而未盡夫惻隱之實。使在聖門，作而成之，可與仲由竝駕也。陳太丘持心最平，而所處張讓之事亦未中節。
translation_en:
…this is what it means to have failed in the way of handling adversity and overcoming difficulty. Nanxuan further said that acclaim for reputation and integrity arises in declining ages. This is because the earlier Confucians had long cultivated abundant learning, which manifested itself as circumstances required. They did not conspicuously assert their integrity [?], yet it could not be wrested from them; they did not conspicuously sacrifice themselves for reputation [?], yet reputation followed them of itself. When the age declined and the Way grew faint, those who could rise above vulgar conventions and stand firm amid decline were credited by the world with reputation and integrity. Gentlemen whose learning of the Way had not yet reached perfection also took pride in these qualities. This does not mean that reputation and integrity were not valued in flourishing ages.

Sima Guang lamented that the men of the partisan proscriptions, born into an age of benighted disorder, could not escape the calamities inflicted by petty men. He particularly approved of Guo Tai and Shentu Pan: the former refrained from perilously outspoken words and provocative arguments, living in a corrupt age without incurring resentment or calamity; the latter acted upon perceiving the first signs of change and, remaining aloof, escaped public criticism. Such indeed is the way of preserving oneself through wisdom and discernment.

When Nanxuan subsequently discussed these events, he placed Li Ying, Du Mi, and Chen Fan in the category of Zhong You, and Chen Shi, Guo Tai, and Huang Xian in that of Yan Hui. This distinction was not without reason. Although the conduct of Li Ying, Du Mi, Chen Fan, and their fellows was upright, and their adherence to integrity strict, their actions were still prompted by spirited indignation rather than proceeding from a settled assurance in moral principle. They arose from the impulse of aversion to hearing cries of suffering, without fully realizing the substance of compassion. Had they studied in the Sage’s school and been inspired and brought to maturity there, they could have stood alongside Zhong You. Chen Shi, known as Chen of Taiqiu, maintained the greatest equanimity of mind, yet his handling of the affair involving Zhang Rang likewise fell short of the proper measure.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
郭有道識量才猷人物冠冕而收斂之□
猶未之盡至於黃叔度言論風旨雖不可
見而氣象溫厚圭角渾然使在聖門作而
成之幾與顔氏一流也是皆惜其天資最
美大道未聞使加以學問之功是亦聖人
之徒非過論也下逮兩晉士懲前軌遂指
黨人以爲口實往往矯枉過正天下靡然
從之風俗淫僻恥尚失所學者以莊老爲
宗而黜六經談者以虛蕩爲辨而賤名檢
===
行身者以放濁爲通而狹節信進仕者以
苟得爲貴而鄙居正當官者以望空爲高
而笑勤恪禮法刑政蕩無一存卒致神州
陸沉中原傾覆王夷甫諸人實爲之倡不
得不任其責也愚甞誦宋儒楊中立之言
曰西漢之士喜功名而不務奇節東漢之
士貴節義而不通時變兩晉之士樂恬曠
而不爭實用真萬世公天下之斷案也執
事乃欲折衷於三者之間以爲居身之珍
punctuated:
郭有道識量才猷，人物冠冕，而收斂之□猶未之盡。至於黃叔度，言論風旨雖不可見，而氣象溫厚，圭角渾然，使在聖門作而成之，幾與顔氏一流也。是皆惜其天資最美，大道未聞，使加以學問之功，是亦聖人之徒，非過論也。下逮兩晉，士懲前軌，遂指黨人以爲口實，往往矯枉過正。天下靡然從之，風俗淫僻，恥尚失所。學者以莊老爲宗而黜六經，談者以虛蕩爲辨而賤名檢，行身者以放濁爲通而狹節信，進仕者以苟得爲貴而鄙居正，當官者以望空爲高而笑勤恪。禮法刑政，蕩無一存，卒致神州陸沉，中原傾覆。王夷甫諸人實爲之倡，不得不任其責也。
愚甞誦宋儒楊中立之言曰：「西漢之士喜功名而不務奇節，東漢之士貴節義而不通時變，兩晉之士樂恬曠而不爭實用。」真萬世公天下之斷案也。執事乃欲折衷於三者之間，以爲居身之珍。
translation_en:
…Guo Youdao stood foremost among men in discernment, breadth of mind, ability, and judgment, yet his practice of self-restraint [?] remained incomplete. As for Huang Shudu, although his words and the tenor of his thought can no longer be ascertained, his bearing was gentle and generous, with no sharp edges showing. Had he been cultivated and brought to maturity in the sage’s school, he would have ranked nearly with Yan Hui. These assessments all express regret that, despite their excellent natural endowments, they had not heard the Great Way. Had they added the work of learning to those endowments, they too would have been followers of the sage. This is no exaggerated judgment.
By the time of the Western and Eastern Jin, scholars, taking warning from earlier precedents, made the men of the proscribed faction their pretext, repeatedly going too far in correcting past errors. All under Heaven followed the prevailing trend. Customs became dissolute and perverse, and people misplaced their shame and esteem. Students took Zhuangzi and Laozi as their masters and rejected the Six Classics. Those engaged in discussion treated empty, unrestrained talk as argument and despised reputation and proper conduct. In their personal behavior, men regarded license and impurity as broad-mindedness, and integrity and trustworthiness as narrowness. Those seeking office prized obtaining it by any means and scorned adherence to rectitude. Those holding office considered gazing into emptiness lofty and laughed at diligence and conscientiousness. Ritual, law, punishments, and government were swept away, leaving nothing intact. In the end, this caused the sacred land of China to sink into ruin and the Central Plain to fall. Wang Yifu and his associates truly led the way in this and cannot escape responsibility.
I have often recited the words of the Song Confucian Yang Zhongli: “The scholars of the Western Han delighted in achievement and fame but did not strive for exceptional integrity. The scholars of the Eastern Han prized integrity and righteousness but failed to understand changing circumstances. The scholars of the Western and Eastern Jin enjoyed tranquil detachment but did not vie to be of practical use.” This is truly an impartial verdict for all under Heaven and for all ages. You now wish to weigh these three approaches and find the proper balance among them, making it a treasure for guiding your own conduct…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
愚何足以知之無已則以明問所及者而
姑繹其義昔羅仲素有曰士立朝要以正
直忠厚爲本正直則朝廷無過失忠厚則
天下無嗟怨二者不可偏廢也又曰士之
立身要以名節忠義爲本有名節則不枉
道以求進有忠義則不固寵以欺君由是
言之則士君子出處進退之間不夷不惠
而持衡之道端不外是聖賢居身之所珍
亦即此在矣尚何患于過中失正以落漢
===
晉之窠臼也哉雖然轉移之機則又係乎
上之人何如耳仲素固曰朝廷有教化則
士人有廉恥士人有廉恥則天下有風俗
嗚呼世道之關係豈淺淺云哉愚也不敏
矢心誓節願獻芹曝有年矣執事倘不鄙
狂斐而進之尚當盡披忠赤而以轉移上
風之機敬陳于
丹陛下
第四問
punctuated:
愚何足以知之？無已，則以明問所及者而姑繹其義。昔羅仲素有曰：「士立朝，要以正直忠厚爲本。正直則朝廷無過失，忠厚則天下無嗟怨，二者不可偏廢也。」又曰：「士之立身，要以名節忠義爲本。有名節則不枉道以求進，有忠義則不固寵以欺君。」由是言之，則士君子出處進退之間，不夷不惠，而持衡之道端不外是。聖賢居身之所珍，亦即此在矣。尚何患于過中失正，以落漢晉之窠臼也哉？雖然，轉移之機則又係乎上之人何如耳。仲素固曰：「朝廷有教化，則士人有廉恥；士人有廉恥，則天下有風俗。」嗚呼！世道之關係，豈淺淺云哉？愚也不敏，矢心誓節，願獻芹曝有年矣。執事倘不鄙狂斐而進之，尚當盡披忠赤，而以轉移上風之機敬陳于丹陛下。

第四問
translation_en:
…How could someone as unlearned as I be adequate to understand this? If I must nevertheless speak, let me provisionally unfold the meaning of what your discerning question addresses. Luo Zhongsu once said: “A scholar serving at court must take uprightness, loyalty, and generosity as his foundation. With uprightness, the court will commit no errors; with loyalty and generosity, there will be no sighs of grievance throughout the realm. Neither may be neglected.” He also said: “In establishing himself, a scholar must take honorable reputation, moral integrity, loyalty, and righteousness as his foundation. With honorable reputation and moral integrity, he will not bend the Way to seek advancement; with loyalty and righteousness, he will not secure his hold on favor by deceiving his ruler.”

Judging from these words, when a gentleman chooses between service and retirement, advancement and withdrawal, he should follow neither the extreme of Bo Yi nor that of Liuxia Hui. The way to maintain a proper balance lies precisely in these principles. Here, too, lies what sages and worthies treasure in conducting themselves. Why, then, fear overstepping the mean and losing rectitude, thereby falling into the ruts of the Han and Jin?

Nevertheless, the possibility of bringing about change also depends on what those above are like. Zhongsu indeed said: “When the court provides moral instruction, scholars have a sense of integrity and shame; when scholars have a sense of integrity and shame, sound customs prevail throughout the realm.” Alas! Can the implications for the moral condition of the age possibly be called slight?

Slow-witted though I am, I have pledged my heart and sworn to preserve my integrity. For years I have wished to offer my humble contribution—as one offers celery or the warmth of the sun. If you, sir, do not disdain these rash and ill-considered words and advance me, I shall lay bare all my loyal sincerity and respectfully present before the vermilion steps of the throne the means of transforming the influence exerted from above.

Fourth Question

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
劉元凱
同考試官教諭林　批　理一分殊孟子辨告子已言
之顧未有能發之者子能據此會聖賢之說而歸之致
紛紛理氣之惑庶其足破乎
同考試官教諭楊　批　異言淆亂折諸心非子吾誰
與歸
考試官學正石　批　學識不易到此
考試官教授李　批　性學斷案足以珍矣
性可以易知乎昔子貢固親師夫子者也
===
猶不得而聞焉果難知乎夫子固曰知止
而后有定止也者性之謂也是知性固學
者之所先矣可以其難而不知耶雖然易
詩書春秋禮樂皆盡性之書而於性且未
之明言也吾夫子為盡性之宗而於性亦
未之明言也由夫子而來談性者則又紛
紛矣是與非其孰從而辨之盖嘗讀孟氏
之書而竊有覺焉其言曰盡其心者知其
性也知其性則知天矣是言乎知性必自
punctuated:
劉元凱

同考試官教諭林　批：理一分殊，孟子辨告子已言之，顧未有能發之者。子能據此會聖賢之說而歸之致，紛紛理氣之惑，庶其足破乎！

同考試官教諭楊　批：異言淆亂，折諸心，非子吾誰與歸？

考試官學正石　批：學識不易到此。

考試官教授李　批：性學斷案，足以珍矣。

性可以易知乎？昔子貢固親師夫子者也，猶不得而聞焉。果難知乎？夫子固曰：「知止而后有定。」止也者，性之謂也。是知性固學者之所先矣，可以其難而不知耶？雖然，《易》《詩》《書》《春秋》《禮》《樂》，皆盡性之書，而於性且未之明言也。吾夫子為盡性之宗，而於性亦未之明言也。由夫子而來，談性者則又紛紛矣。是與非，其孰從而辨之？盖嘗讀孟氏之書，而竊有覺焉。其言曰：「盡其心者，知其性也；知其性，則知天矣。」是言乎知性必自
translation_en:
Liu Yuankai

Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor, comments: “Principle is one, but its particular manifestations differ. Mencius already stated this in his refutation of Gaozi, yet no one has been able to elucidate it. You have used this insight to reconcile the teachings of the sages and worthies and bring them to a common purport [?]. Might this suffice to dispel the manifold confusions concerning principle and material force?”

Associate Examiner Yang, Instructor, comments: “Divergent teachings sow confusion; you adjudicate them through the heart-mind. If not with you, with whom should I stand?”

Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: “It is no easy matter for learning and discernment to reach this level.”

Examiner Li, Professor, comments: “A definitive judgment in the study of human nature, well worthy of being treasured.”

Can human nature be readily known? In former times, Zigong studied personally under the Master, yet even he could not hear the Master speak of it. Is it indeed difficult to know? The Master certainly said: “Only after knowing where to stop can one have a settled purpose.” This stopping point refers to human nature. Thus, knowing human nature is surely the learner’s first priority. Can we leave it unknown merely because it is difficult? Nevertheless, the Changes, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, Rites, and Music are all books that fully realize human nature, yet they do not explicitly speak of it. Our Master was the supreme exemplar of fully realizing human nature, yet he too did not explicitly speak of it. Since the Master’s time, those who discuss human nature have offered a profusion of views. By what means can we distinguish right from wrong among them? I once read the book of Mencius and privately gained an insight. He says: “Those who fully develop their heart-mind know their nature. Knowing their nature, they know Heaven.” This means that knowing human nature must begin with …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
盡心始也然則孟氏之言性善也顧嘗由
盡心而知之者乎周程二子不疑於孟氏
而容有異焉者顧皆嘗由盡心而得之者
乎自餘紛紛或出焉或入焉而未足以取
信於天下者則固强探力索之過也已且
夫一陰一陽之謂道也繼之者善也成之
者性也非語性之源乎仁者見之謂之仁
知者見之謂之知百姓日用而不知也非
語夫源之同而其流之異乎性相近也習
===
相遠也上智下愚之不移也固即夫性之
流而言之者也夫源與流弗可二焉者也
天命氣質之論上稽諸夫子而下揆諸周
程無亦容有所未盡乎今夫性也者即道
也道果何物哉昔夫子懼天下之不知也
曰一陰一陽之謂道陰陽氣也一陰焉又
一陽焉言夫陰陽之合體也言夫氣之混
合陰陽而不偏也是故即氣即道也故夫
子曰乾道變化各正性命保合太和太和
punctuated:
盡心始也。然則孟氏之言性善也，顧嘗由盡心而知之者乎？周程二子不疑於孟氏，而容有異焉者，顧皆嘗由盡心而得之者乎？自餘紛紛，或出焉，或入焉，而未足以取信於天下者，則固强探力索之過也已。且夫「一陰一陽之謂道也，繼之者善也，成之者性也」，非語性之源乎？「仁者見之謂之仁，知者見之謂之知，百姓日用而不知也」，非語夫源之同而其流之異乎？「性相近也，習相遠也」，「上智下愚之不移也」，固即夫性之流而言之者也。夫源與流，弗可二焉者也。天命氣質之論，上稽諸夫子，而下揆諸周程，無亦容有所未盡乎？

今夫性也者，即道也。道果何物哉？昔夫子懼天下之不知也，曰：「一陰一陽之謂道。」陰陽，氣也。一陰焉，又一陽焉，言夫陰陽之合體也，言夫氣之混合陰陽而不偏也。是故即氣即道也。故夫子曰：「乾道變化，各正性命，保合太和。」太和
translation_en:
…begins with fully realizing one’s heart-mind. If so, when Master Meng spoke of human nature as good, had he indeed come to know this by fully realizing his heart-mind? The two masters, Zhou and Cheng, did not doubt Master Meng, yet allowed for differences: had they both likewise arrived at their understanding by fully realizing their heart-minds? As for the multitude of other disputants, some departing from his teaching and some adhering to it, who have failed to win the trust of the world, their fault surely lies in forcing their inquiries and straining their investigations. Moreover, does not the statement, “One yin and one yang are called the Way; what continues it is goodness, and what completes it is nature,” speak of the source of nature? Does not the statement, “The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom; the common people use it daily without knowing it,” speak of a common source whose streams differ? “By nature people are close to one another; through habituation they grow far apart,” and “The highest in wisdom and the lowest in foolishness do not change”: these surely speak of nature in its downstream manifestations. Yet source and stream cannot be treated as two separate things. If we examine the discourse on Heaven-endowed nature and the nature of one’s material constitution against Confucius above and assess it against Zhou and Cheng below, might there still be something it has not fully accounted for?

Now nature is precisely the Way. What, indeed, is the Way? In former times, Confucius, fearing that the world would not understand it, said: “One yin and one yang are called the Way.” Yin and yang are qi, material force. To speak of one yin and then one yang is to speak of their forming a single body; it is to say that qi blends yin and yang without being partial to either. Thus qi itself is the Way. Hence Confucius said: “The Way of Qian transforms and changes; each thing attains its proper nature and allotted destiny, preserving and uniting in Supreme Harmony.” Supreme Harmony…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
即性命也又曰大哉乾乎剛健中正純粹
精也夫乾陽也剛健中正純粹精以言乎
其爲天德也故道也者即氣也人性有智
愚賢不肖之不同也可謂其非天命乎夫
源與流又胡爲乎異也今夫太和運而陰
陽分陰陽流而剛柔之變於是乎萬有不
齊矣剛柔之變萬有不齊而夫人之性也
豈得而盡同乎故一剛一柔之不同者此
其大分也自剛柔之大分而又別之則剛
===
善剛惡柔善柔惡剛中柔中又若是乎其
不同矣夫以言乎其稟受也則固惟有剛
柔之偏與剛柔之中耳就其剛柔之偏又
惟有多寡參差之分不盡同焉而已耳而
可以惡言乎自其形生神發之後而觀之
則隨其剛柔之偏與中多與寡而善與惡
中與不中之類判矣故程子曰人生而靜
以上不容說纔說性時便已不是性也此
其確論也蓋非不是性也謂非性之初也
punctuated: 即性命也。又曰：「大哉乾乎！剛健中正純粹精也。」夫乾，陽也。剛健中正純粹精，以言乎其爲天德也。故道也者，即氣也。人性有智愚賢不肖之不同也，可謂其非天命乎？夫源與流，又胡爲乎異也？今夫太和運而陰陽分，陰陽流而剛柔之變，於是乎萬有不齊矣。剛柔之變，萬有不齊，而夫人之性也，豈得而盡同乎？故一剛一柔之不同者，此其大分也。自剛柔之大分而又別之，則剛善、剛惡、柔善、柔惡、剛中、柔中，又若是乎其不同矣。夫以言乎其稟受也，則固惟有剛柔之偏與剛柔之中耳。就其剛柔之偏，又惟有多寡參差之分，不盡同焉而已耳，而可以惡言乎？自其形生神發之後而觀之，則隨其剛柔之偏與中、多與寡，而善與惡、中與不中之類判矣。故程子曰：「人生而靜以上不容說，纔說性時，便已不是性也。」此其確論也。蓋非不是性也，謂非性之初也。
translation_en:
…is precisely nature and the heavenly endowment. It further says: “Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure, unmixed, and quintessential.” Qian is yang. “Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure, unmixed, and quintessential” describes its being the virtue of Heaven. Thus the Way is precisely qi. Human nature differs in wisdom and foolishness, worthiness and unworthiness: can one say that it is not Heaven’s endowment? Why, then, should source and stream be different?

Now, as the Great Harmony moves, yin and yang differentiate; as yin and yang flow, transformations of firmness and yielding arise, and the myriad things become unequal. With these transformations of firmness and yielding and the resulting inequalities among the myriad things, how could human natures all be identical? Thus the difference between being firm and being yielding is their principal division. If further distinctions are made within this principal division, there are firmness that is good, firmness that is evil, yielding that is good, yielding that is evil, firmness that attains the mean, and yielding that attains the mean. Such, again, are their differences.

Yet in speaking of what people receive as their endowment, there is certainly only a partial inclination toward firmness or yielding, or a balanced mean between them. Within such partial inclinations, there are merely differences of greater and lesser amounts, unevenly distributed and not entirely alike. Can these be described as evil? If we observe people after their bodily form has come into being and their spirit has become active, then, according to the partiality or balance of their firmness and yielding, and their greater or lesser amounts, distinctions emerge between the good and the evil, those who attain the mean and those who do not.

Thus Master Cheng said: “What precedes ‘At birth, human beings are still’ cannot be spoken of. As soon as one speaks of nature, it is already no longer nature.” This is his definitive judgment. He does not mean that it is not nature; he means that it is not nature in its initial state.

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
故又曰善惡皆天理善固性也惡亦不可
不謂之性也此皆其灼見而言之者歟夫
孟子之言性也則自夫形生神發之後而
言之也何專言乎善耶孟子固曰盡其心
者知其性也誠欲知孟子之不誣也曷自
其盡心而驗之乎蓋夫天地之性也動而
無動焉靜而無靜焉動靜合一而未始離
也故曰無聲無臭也坱然太虛也是故剛
矣變而爲柔柔矣變而爲剛剛柔不居也
===
固神之爲也夫其形生神發也感於物而
動靜斯離矣動靜離則剛柔之性固已涉
於聲臭而非神於是乎剛柔善惡判而非
復天地之性矣然固非果二於初也以夫
動靜離而二於初也盡心也者卽孔子所
謂敬以直周子所謂一爲要程子所謂約
其情使合於中蓋卽吾剛柔善惡之性而
復乎吾動而無動靜而無靜之初也動靜
合一之初果復則虛圓湛一之神全而聰
punctuated: 故又曰：「善惡皆天理。善固性也，惡亦不可不謂之性也。」此皆其灼見而言之者歟！夫孟子之言性也，則自夫形生神發之後而言之也，何專言乎善耶？孟子固曰：「盡其心者，知其性也。」誠欲知孟子之不誣也，曷自其盡心而驗之乎？蓋夫天地之性也，動而無動焉，靜而無靜焉，動靜合一而未始離也。故曰：「無聲無臭也，坱然太虛也。」是故剛矣，變而爲柔；柔矣，變而爲剛。剛柔不居也，固神之爲也。夫其形生神發也，感於物而動靜斯離矣。動靜離，則剛柔之性固已涉於聲臭而非神，於是乎剛柔善惡判，而非復天地之性矣。然固非果二於初也，以夫動靜離而二於初也。盡心也者，卽孔子所謂敬以直、周子所謂一爲要、程子所謂約其情使合於中，蓋卽吾剛柔善惡之性而復乎吾動而無動、靜而無靜之初也。動靜合一之初果復，則虛圓湛一之神全而聰
translation_en: Thus Master Cheng also said: “Good and evil are both heavenly principle. Good is certainly human nature, but evil, too, cannot be said not to be human nature.” Surely these statements all arose from his penetrating insight! Now, when Mengzi spoke of human nature, he spoke of it after bodily form had come into being and spirit had become active. Why, then, did he speak exclusively of goodness? Mengzi himself said: “One who fully realizes his heart knows his nature.” If we truly wish to know that Mengzi’s words were not false, why not test them by fully realizing the heart? For the nature of Heaven and Earth moves without movement and is still without stillness; movement and stillness are united and have never been separate. Hence it is said: “It has neither sound nor smell; it is the boundless Great Void.” Thus, what is firm changes into what is yielding, and what is yielding changes into what is firm. Firmness and yielding do not remain fixed: this is indeed the working of spirit. Once bodily form comes into being and spirit becomes active, responses to things cause movement and stillness to separate. When movement and stillness separate, the nature characterized by firmness and yielding has already entered the realm of sound and smell and is no longer spirit. Firmness and yielding, goodness and evil, then become distinct, and this is no longer the nature of Heaven and Earth. Yet it is not truly something different from its original state; it differs from that state because movement and stillness have separated. Fully realizing the heart is precisely what Kongzi meant by “using reverence to make upright,” what Master Zhou meant by “taking oneness as essential,” and what Master Cheng meant by “restraining the feelings so that they accord with the mean.” It means returning, through this very nature of ours with its firmness and yielding, goodness and evil, to our original state of moving without movement and being still without stillness. If that original unity of movement and stillness is indeed restored, then the spirit, empty, rounded, limpid, and undivided, is whole, and perceptiveness…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
明睿智之幾發剛之惡者化而剛之善者
中矣柔之惡者化而柔之善者中矣於玆
而驗之將信其果善乎否也是故孟子曰
求則得之舍則失之仁義禮智之性固未
嘗言不待求而得也亦未嘗言不待盡而
知也故孟子之專言善也周程二子與之
同而容有異也異言而同旨者也皆眞有
得於孔氏者也張子知太和爲道而乃有
形而後有氣質之性之說或者詞偶出入
===
而旨固未嘗支也朱子因之或者偶未嘗
究極言之耳豈固二於周程二子哉昔告
子以生之謂性也孟子詰之而闢其非闢
其非者以其謂人與牛馬之性一也由是
觀之性一而分殊源一而流殊就其分之
殊而反其湛一之機而性之源即在焉合
孟子全書而觀之蓋虀虀乎未始與吾夫
子二也先儒以其功之配禹也不亦宜哉
雖然非從事乎盡心之訓而實有見乎吾
punctuated: 明睿智之幾發，剛之惡者化，而剛之善者中矣；柔之惡者化，而柔之善者中矣。於玆而驗之，將信其果善乎否也。是故孟子曰：「求則得之，舍則失之。」仁義禮智之性，固未嘗言不待求而得也，亦未嘗言不待盡而知也。故孟子之專言善也，周程二子與之同，而容有異也，異言而同旨者也，皆眞有得於孔氏者也。張子知太和爲道，而乃有「形而後有氣質之性」之說，或者詞偶出入，而旨固未嘗支也。朱子因之，或者偶未嘗究極言之耳，豈固二於周程二子哉！昔告子以生之謂性也，孟子詰之而闢其非。闢其非者，以其謂人與牛馬之性一也。由是觀之，性一而分殊，源一而流殊。就其分之殊，而反其湛一之機，而性之源即在焉。合孟子全書而觀之，蓋虀虀乎未始與吾夫子二也。先儒以其功之配禹也，不亦宜哉！雖然，非從事乎盡心之訓，而實有見乎吾
translation_en:
…the incipient workings of understanding and wisdom emerge. What is evil in firmness is transformed, and what is good in firmness attains due measure; what is evil in yielding is transformed, and what is good in yielding attains due measure. If we test it at this point, we shall ascertain whether human nature is indeed good. Thus Mengzi said: “Seek it and you obtain it; abandon it and you lose it.” As for the nature endowed with benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom, he never said that it could be attained without seeking, nor that it could be known without fully realizing it. Thus, in Mengzi’s exclusive emphasis on goodness, the two masters Zhou Dunyi and Cheng Yi agree with him, though differences may be admitted: their words differ, but their intent is the same. All truly grasped the teaching of Confucius.

Master Zhang Zai knew that Supreme Harmony was the Way, yet he also advanced the statement that “only after there is bodily form is there a nature constituted by material endowment.” Perhaps his wording occasionally varies, but his intent never diverges. Master Zhu Xi followed him; perhaps he simply did not, on that occasion, explain the matter exhaustively. How could he fundamentally differ from the two masters Zhou and Cheng?

Formerly, Gaozi held that what is inborn is called nature. Mengzi challenged him and refuted his error. He refuted him because Gaozi held that the nature of humans was identical to that of oxen and horses. Viewed in this light, nature is one, but its particular manifestations differ; the source is one, but its streams differ. Starting from these differing manifestations, return to the incipient workings of its limpid unity: there lies the source of nature. Considering the book of Mengzi as a whole, we find that it [?] never differed from our Master Confucius. Was it not fitting that earlier Confucian scholars regarded Mengzi’s achievement as equal to that of Yu? Nevertheless, unless one applies oneself to the teaching of fully realizing the mind and actually gains insight into our …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
性之眞雖其說之已詳固猶影響而已耳
愚非深造自得者也偶得其似而言之而
近與否固不自知也惟執事其進教之
第五問
方正脩
同考試官教諭沈　批〔天下事無常形夷狄之盛衰向背亦無定勢應變審幾乃其要也子能條陳畫一而無遺策〕
〔末復歸重于內治之脩得之爲上尤知體要所謂識時務之俊傑非子也耶〕
考試官學正石　批〔以通變立論以李張二公治蜀之政爲脩攘之要最識馭夷先後之著是用録出〕
===
考試官教授李　批〔蜀中夷情制馭之良法是如此〕
盡制而曲防者靖邊之要道相時而更議
者通變之遠猷夫夷狄之爲吾邊患凡以
邊防闊踈控制匪人乘間作孽故態然也
況夫事無常形夷無定性當事者乃安于
故常執成說而憚更張樂因循以諱邊事
吾恐幾會坐失事變莫圖邊患之日殷而
punctuated:
性之眞，雖其說之已詳，固猶影響而已耳。愚非深造自得者也，偶得其似而言之，而近與否，固不自知也。惟執事其進教之。

第五問
方正脩
同考試官教諭沈，批〔天下事無常形，夷狄之盛衰向背亦無定勢，應變審幾乃其要也。子能條陳畫一而無遺策，末復歸重于內治之脩，得之爲上，尤知體要。所謂識時務之俊傑，非子也耶？〕
考試官學正石，批〔以通變立論，以李張二公治蜀之政爲脩攘之要，最識馭夷先後之著，是用録出。〕
考試官教授李，批〔蜀中夷情，制馭之良法，是如此。〕

盡制而曲防者，靖邊之要道；相時而更議者，通變之遠猷。夫夷狄之爲吾邊患，凡以邊防闊踈，控制匪人，乘間作孽，故態然也。況夫事無常形，夷無定性，當事者乃安于故常，執成說而憚更張，樂因循以諱邊事。吾恐幾會坐失，事變莫圖，邊患之日殷而
translation_en:
…the truth of our nature—even though the explanation is already detailed, it remains no more than shadows and echoes. I am not one who has attained deep understanding through study and made it his own. Having chanced upon something resembling it, I have ventured to speak; whether my account comes close, I myself do not know. I ask that you favor me with further instruction.

Fifth Question
Fang Zhengxiu

Associate Examiner Shen, Instructor, comments: 〔Affairs in the world have no constant form, and the strength or weakness, allegiance or hostility of the non-Han peoples likewise follow no fixed pattern. Responding to change and discerning incipient developments are therefore essential. You have set out your proposals systematically, omitting no measure. At the end you again place the emphasis on improving internal administration, rightly treating this as paramount: you understand especially well the essentials. Are you not precisely what is meant by an outstanding man who understands the affairs of his time?〕

Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔You base your argument on adapting to change, and take the administration of Sichuan by Lords Li and Zhang as the essentials of internal improvement and resistance to outside threats. You understand exceptionally well the sequence of measures for managing the non-Han peoples. For this reason, your answer has been selected for inclusion.〕

Examiner Li, Professor, comments: 〔Given the circumstances of the non-Han peoples in Sichuan, sound methods for controlling and managing them are indeed as described here.〕

To exercise control comprehensively and take precautions in every particular is the essential way to pacify the frontier; to assess the times and reconsider policy is the far-sighted strategy for adapting to change. That the non-Han peoples cause trouble on our frontiers is entirely because frontier defenses are lax and those entrusted with control are unsuitable. They seize opportunities to make trouble: this is their habitual behavior. Moreover, affairs have no constant form, and these peoples have no fixed disposition. Yet those responsible rest content with established practice, cling to received opinions and shrink from reform, and gladly persist in routine while avoiding discussion of frontier affairs. I fear that opportunities will be lost through inaction, that no plans will be made for changing circumstances, and that frontier troubles will grow ever more severe, and…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
生民禍亂寧有旣乎然則通其變以捄其
偏以輔乎法之不逮乃今日籌邊第一義
也知此則川東諸夷控馭之道可以稍倣
西南而今日建閫之議可謂坐得勝筭也
矣愚也生長古梁憂切邊患固嘗問諸將
校受之故老頗悉夷情之顚末玆承下問
敢不竊効芻蕘用備葑菲嗟哉吾蜀之民
也爰自蠶叢開國世罹邊禍壯士懷鋒鏑
之憂閭右竭轉輸之力左右皆坑谷前後
===
一網罟誠無所逃于天地之間三方土夷
均之爲吾蜀之患也審矣而執事顧以川
東深念視西南若在所畧焉夫豈不以西
南諸夷先後之所建明上下之所經略已
有得于長駕遠馭之道乎今夫如專閫之
寄畀之總戎分閫之任責之裨副當關有
夫也誰何有人也而又分遣憲臣兼制共
事而彈壓于其境焉文經武緯代不乏人
馭夷之策奇正咸備先時大比蓋嘗發爲
punctuated: 生民禍亂寧有旣乎？然則通其變以捄其偏，以輔乎法之不逮，乃今日籌邊第一義也。知此，則川東諸夷控馭之道可以稍倣西南，而今日建閫之議可謂坐得勝筭也矣。愚也生長古梁，憂切邊患，固嘗問諸將校，受之故老，頗悉夷情之顚末。玆承下問，敢不竊効芻蕘，用備葑菲？嗟哉！吾蜀之民也，爰自蠶叢開國，世罹邊禍。壯士懷鋒鏑之憂，閭右竭轉輸之力，左右皆坑谷，前後一網罟，誠無所逃于天地之間。三方土夷，均之爲吾蜀之患也審矣，而執事顧以川東深念，視西南若在所畧焉。夫豈不以西南諸夷，先後之所建明，上下之所經略，已有得于長駕遠馭之道乎？今夫如專閫之寄，畀之總戎；分閫之任，責之裨副。當關有夫也，誰何有人也，而又分遣憲臣，兼制共事，而彈壓于其境焉。文經武緯，代不乏人；馭夷之策，奇正咸備。先時大比，蓋嘗發爲
translation_en:
…could there ever be an end to the calamities and disorder suffered by the people? Thus, adapting to changing circumstances to remedy shortcomings and supplement what established regulations cannot achieve is the foremost principle in planning frontier affairs today. Once this is understood, methods for controlling the various non-Han peoples of eastern Sichuan can to some extent follow those used in the southwest; the present proposal to establish a military command may then be said to secure a winning strategy without leaving one's seat.

I, in my ignorance, was born and raised in the ancient region of Liang and am deeply concerned about frontier troubles. I have indeed questioned military officers and received instruction from venerable elders, gaining a fair understanding of the circumstances of these peoples from beginning to end. Now that you have condescended to ask, how could I fail to offer my humble counsel, like that of a grass-cutter or wood-gatherer, for whatever little worth you may find in it?

Alas for the people of our Shu! Ever since Cancong founded his kingdom, generation after generation has suffered frontier calamities. Stalwart men live in fear of blades and arrowheads, while wealthy households exhaust their resources transporting supplies. To left and right are pits and ravines; before and behind, one enclosing net. Truly there is nowhere between Heaven and Earth to escape. It is certain that the indigenous non-Han peoples on all three sides alike pose a threat to our Shu. Yet you, sir, give particular thought to eastern Sichuan and seem to leave the southwest out of account. Is this not because, concerning the various non-Han peoples of the southwest, the measures proposed successively and the planning undertaken by superior and subordinate officials have already achieved effective methods of controlling them over great distances?

As matters now stand, responsibility for an independent regional command is entrusted to a regional commander, and responsibility for subordinate commands is assigned to assistant and deputy commanders. There are men to hold the passes and men to challenge those who approach. Moreover, censorial officials are separately dispatched to exercise concurrent control, work together, and keep order within the territory. Civil administration provides the warp and military affairs the weft, and successive generations have lacked no capable men. Strategies for controlling the non-Han peoples include both unconventional and conventional methods. At an earlier Provincial Examination, this was once set as…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
問目策我蜀士固已上之主司獻之
天子之廷推行有漸迄今賴之惟夫川東之夷
則有可議者蓋受命
王朝官其酋長與西南同也犬羊成性豺虎
滋毒邊禍同于西南也則夫建閫設官揆
之事體宜若無異同者何彼然而此獨不
然無亦此猶稍近腹裏而彼則西鄰吐蕃
南接南詔爲邊徼之重地勢固爾殊也殊
不知當時發謀之初固未至如今日之多
===
事也自今觀之酉陽石硅介在湖省之間
日與溪峒諸蠻迭相雄長播邑平茶連絡
貴竹之凱里禍端之啓曾不旋踵或以民
夷互市小爭以言或以土地相侵大爭以
兵甚至劫奪民財掠及子女又甚而依負
岩險戕我官兵羽書突至于官司飛語動
干乎兩省迨夫詞以理屈輒爾撫拾草言
欺罔
天聽以圖遷延倖脫至有十數年不了之案推
punctuated:
問目，策我蜀士，固已上之主司，獻之天子之廷，推行有漸，迄今賴之。惟夫川東之夷，則有可議者。蓋受命王朝，官其酋長，與西南同也；犬羊成性，豺虎滋毒，邊禍同于西南也。則夫建閫設官，揆之事體，宜若無異同者。何彼然而此獨不然？無亦此猶稍近腹裏，而彼則西鄰吐蕃，南接南詔，爲邊徼之重，地勢固爾殊也？殊不知當時發謀之初，固未至如今日之多事也。
自今觀之，酉陽、石硅介在湖省之間，日與溪峒諸蠻迭相雄長；播邑、平茶連絡貴竹之凱里，禍端之啓，曾不旋踵。或以民夷互市，小爭以言；或以土地相侵，大爭以兵。甚至劫奪民財，掠及子女；又甚而依負岩險，戕我官兵。羽書突至于官司，飛語動干乎兩省。迨夫詞以理屈，輒爾撫拾草言，欺罔天聽，以圖遷延倖脫，至有十數年不了之案。推
translation_en:
…as examination questions to test our scholars of Shu. Their proposals have already been submitted to the chief examiners and presented at the court of the Son of Heaven. They have gradually been put into practice, and we continue to benefit from them today. Yet there is something to discuss concerning the non-Han peoples of eastern Sichuan. Their chieftains receive appointments from the imperial court and hold official rank, just as those in the southwest do. Their nature is that of dogs and sheep, and they spread harm like jackals and tigers; the troubles they cause on the frontier are likewise the same as those in the southwest. Thus, judged by the circumstances, establishing military commands and appointing officials ought to follow the same arrangements. Why are these arrangements adopted there alone, but not here? Is it perhaps because this region lies somewhat closer to the interior, whereas the other borders Tufan to the west and Nanzhao to the south, occupying a crucial position on the frontier, so that their geographical situations are indeed different? This overlooks the fact that, when those plans were first devised, affairs had certainly not yet become as troubled as they are today.
Looking at the present situation, Youyang and Shigui 石硅 [?] lie along the interface with Huguang Province, daily vying for supremacy with the various non-Han peoples of the streams and mountain valleys. Bo and Pingcha are connected with Kaili in Guizhu, and trouble can erupt in an instant. Sometimes trade between commoners and non-Han peoples gives rise to minor disputes fought with words; sometimes encroachments upon land produce major conflicts fought with weapons. Matters even reach the point of plundering commoners’ property and abducting their sons and daughters. Worse still, they take refuge in rocky strongholds and kill our officers and soldiers. Urgent military dispatches suddenly arrive at government offices, and flying rumors repeatedly embroil the two provinces. When their arguments prove untenable, they gather up flimsy assertions [?] to deceive the imperial ear, hoping to prolong proceedings and escape punishment by good fortune. There are even cases that remain unresolved for more than ten years. Tracing…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
厥所由實以施州衛爲之淵藪唐厓沙溪
諸司助之虎翼蓋該衛名雖統轄實則表
裏爲奸以致兩省會勘之官接踵于道株
守經年撫機興歎末如之何徒以羈縻虛
名遥制難及文移往復動有關礙事勢蓋
甚有難爲處者此耳其諸播凱事勢大略
相當此有識者所以欲通其變以捄其偏
弊者此也邇聞兩省當道移文會議欲於
施州衛
===
奏設將臣一員專制川湖兩界夷情及議將
四川分廵官
奏帶兵備請以
璽書從事兼制播凱庶乎脉絡通貫而腹心之
疾漸可除治臂指相使而萑苻之寇可以
招麾自是上下文移或朝發而夕可以達
奸細亡命或私入而公可以俘其建閫設
鎮雖不必盡如西南事體亦小異而大同
矣誠以西南夷情猶統于一省無掣肘之
punctuated:
厥所由，實以施州衛爲之淵藪，唐厓、沙溪諸司助之虎翼。蓋該衛名雖統轄，實則表裏爲奸，以致兩省會勘之官接踵于道，株守經年，撫機興歎，末如之何。徒以羈縻虛名，遥制難及，文移往復，動有關礙，事勢蓋甚有難爲處者此耳。其諸播凱事勢，大略相當。此有識者所以欲通其變，以捄其偏弊者，此也。
邇聞兩省當道移文會議，欲於施州衛奏設將臣一員，專制川湖兩界夷情；及議將四川分廵官奏帶兵備，請以璽書從事，兼制播凱。庶乎脉絡通貫，而腹心之疾漸可除治；臂指相使，而萑苻之寇可以招麾。自是上下文移，或朝發而夕可以達；奸細亡命，或私入而公可以俘。其建閫設鎮，雖不必盡如西南事體，亦小異而大同矣。誠以西南夷情猶統于一省，無掣肘之
translation_en:
…the underlying cause is, in truth, that Shizhou Guard serves as their refuge, while the offices of Tangya, Shaxi, and elsewhere give them wings like those of a tiger. Although the Guard nominally exercises jurisdiction, in reality those within and outside it collude in wrongdoing. Consequently, officials from the two provinces dispatched to conduct joint investigations follow one another along the roads, remain stranded at their posts for years, and sigh over their desks [?], powerless to act. With only the empty name of loose rein administration, effective control from afar is beyond reach; official correspondence goes back and forth, encountering obstacles at every turn. Herein lies the particular difficulty of handling these affairs. The circumstances in Bozhou and Kaili are broadly similar. This is why discerning men wish to adapt arrangements to changing circumstances and remedy their imbalances and abuses.
Recently I have heard that the authorities of the two provinces have exchanged official communications and held joint deliberations. They intend to memorialize the throne requesting the appointment of one military commander at Shizhou Guard, with sole authority over affairs concerning the non-Han peoples along the Sichuan–Huguang border. They have also discussed requesting that the Sichuan circuit intendant concurrently assume military defense duties, acting under an imperial letter bearing the sovereign’s seal and exercising authority over Bozhou and Kaili as well. It is hoped that the channels of administration will thereby be connected throughout, allowing the disease at the heart of the body gradually to be cured; that commands will pass as readily as from arm to finger, allowing the bandits of the marshes to be summoned and brought under direction. Henceforth, communications between higher and lower authorities might be dispatched in the morning and arrive by evening; spies and fugitives might enter secretly but be captured by the authorities. Although establishing this military headquarters and garrison command need not follow southwestern arrangements in every respect, the differences would be minor and the similarities substantial. Indeed, affairs concerning the non-Han peoples of the southwest still fall under a single province, without the hindrance of…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
虞而川東則介在兩省之間未免有觀望
推諉之弊此創議設官之意斷斷爲不易
之論不得已之舉也雖然尼父以遠人之
服本于內治之脩是蓋不以武備爲尚而
以文德爲先所謂文德亦曰脩民事而示
以綏懷之道是已則今日內治當脩宜先
責諸司牧平互市之訟以息民夷之爭嚴
保伍之法以掛夷夏之界庶民夷各安其
所釁隙無自而生此最爲先著也其次莫
===
過於脩城郭練士卒實軍儲厲器械多立
營堡慎遣戍守嗣是而猶或作亂特舉而
加之以戰以守動罔不利矣此其爲後圖
亦不可忽也考之前史昔李德裕節度西
川建籌邊一樓取西南二道山川之險要
爲夷虜出沒之所者繪圖其上日召諳邊
之士相與商確邊務於是汰冗兵廣招募
請甲人於安定弓人於河中弩人於浙西
而又歸糧運於先春不使涉乎炎瘴驅浮
punctuated:
虞，而川東則介在兩省之間，未免有觀望推諉之弊。此創議設官之意，斷斷爲不易之論、不得已之舉也。雖然，尼父以遠人之服本于內治之脩，是蓋不以武備爲尚，而以文德爲先。所謂文德，亦曰脩民事而示以綏懷之道是已。則今日內治當脩，宜先責諸司牧，平互市之訟，以息民夷之爭；嚴保伍之法，以掛夷夏之界。庶民夷各安其所，釁隙無自而生，此最爲先著也。其次莫過於脩城郭、練士卒、實軍儲、厲器械，多立營堡，慎遣戍守。嗣是而猶或作亂，特舉而加之，以戰以守，動罔不利矣。此其爲後圖，亦不可忽也。
考之前史，昔李德裕節度西川，建籌邊一樓，取西南二道山川之險要，爲夷虜出沒之所者，繪圖其上，日召諳邊之士，相與商確邊務。於是汰冗兵，廣招募，請甲人於安定、弓人於河中、弩人於浙西，而又歸糧運於先春，不使涉乎炎瘴，驅浮
translation_en:
…cause for concern, whereas eastern Sichuan lies between two provinces, making hesitation and the shirking of responsibility difficult to avoid. Such is the intent behind this proposal to establish an official post: it is decidedly a sound argument and a measure made necessary by circumstances. Nevertheless, Confucius held that the submission of distant peoples rests upon the proper ordering of internal government. This surely means giving precedence to civil virtue rather than prizing military preparedness. What is meant by civil virtue is simply attending to the people's affairs and showing them the way of pacification and conciliation. To put internal government in order today, we should first hold the local administrators responsible: settle litigation arising from frontier trade so as to end disputes between the common people and the non-Han peoples, and enforce strictly the system of mutually responsible household groups so as to maintain the boundary between non-Han and Chinese populations [?]. Thus each may remain secure in their own place, leaving no opening for conflict to arise. This is the most urgent first measure. Next, nothing is more important than repairing city walls, training soldiers, replenishing military stores, putting weapons and equipment in good condition, establishing more fortified camps, and carefully assigning garrison troops. If disturbances should still arise thereafter, we need only mobilize forces against them; whether attacking or defending, every action will be advantageous. These subsequent preparations, too, must not be neglected.
Looking to earlier histories, when Li Deyu served as Military Commissioner of Xichuan, he built a tower for planning frontier affairs. He had maps drawn there of the strategic mountains and rivers in the two circuits to the west and south, where non-Han raiders appeared and disappeared. Every day he summoned men familiar with the frontier to deliberate together on frontier affairs. He then discharged superfluous troops and recruited widely, requesting armorers from Anding, bow makers from Hezhong, and crossbow makers from Zhexi. Moreover, he arranged for grain transport before spring, so that those transporting it would not have to pass through the oppressive heat and pestilential mists, and drove the idle…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
層於農畝不使耗乎民財卒之謀定功成
二邊畏悚南詔歸其俘掠伸謀全以城降
此其明效也張詠知成都時以蜀地游食
者衆稍遇水旱民即艱食乃倣常平遺法
以行平糴之政秋稔則出錢易穀儲之官
廩至春則計口給券俾輸元估糴之行之
逾久游惰歸農不入夷境郡以大治而又
篤孝義以惇風俗明約信以濟恩威于時
城中屯兵三萬缺食半月即倉卒以鹽易
===
米克濟其乏主帥玩寇殃民則擒其門吏
責之庭下即日爲之出師卒之兩川平治
詠之力也其諸英烈異政談者韙之夫以
李德裕講武而不廢文德張詠脩文而不
廢武事文武兼資迭施而時出之皆二公
巳試之方也舉而行之有不宜于今日乎
第愚無文饒忠定其人耳誠有之而政焉
有不舉之理哉愚也家世蜀人情鍾桑梓
事切門庭一得之見蓋有誼不容于嘿者
punctuated:
層於農畝，不使耗乎民財。卒之謀定功成，二邊畏悚，南詔歸其俘掠，伸謀全以城降，此其明效也。張詠知成都時，以蜀地游食者衆，稍遇水旱，民即艱食，乃倣常平遺法，以行平糴之政。秋稔則出錢易穀，儲之官廩；至春則計口給券，俾輸元估糴之。行之逾久，游惰歸農，不入夷境，郡以大治。而又篤孝義以惇風俗，明約信以濟恩威。于時城中屯兵三萬，缺食半月，即倉卒以鹽易米，克濟其乏。主帥玩寇殃民，則擒其門吏，責之庭下，即日爲之出師。卒之兩川平治，詠之力也。其諸英烈異政，談者韙之。
夫以李德裕講武而不廢文德，張詠脩文而不廢武事，文武兼資，迭施而時出之，皆二公巳試之方也。舉而行之，有不宜于今日乎？第愚無文饒、忠定其人耳。誠有之，而政焉有不舉之理哉？愚也家世蜀人，情鍾桑梓，事切門庭，一得之見，蓋有誼不容于嘿者
translation_en:
…[putting the idle population?] to work in the fields, so that they would not consume the people’s wealth. In the end, his plans were settled and his undertakings succeeded. Both frontiers were struck with fear; Nanzhao returned those it had captured and what it had plundered, and Shen Mouquan [?] surrendered his city. These were the clear results of his measures.
When Zhang Yong was prefect of Chengdu, he recognized that many people in Shu lived without productive employment, and that even a slight flood or drought left the people hard pressed for food. He therefore followed the surviving methods of the Ever-Normal Granaries and implemented a policy of purchasing grain at fair prices. When the autumn harvest was abundant, he paid out money to purchase grain and stored it in government granaries. In spring, he issued vouchers according to the number of mouths, allowing people to buy the grain at its original price. As this policy continued, the idle returned to farming and no longer entered the territories of the non-Chinese peoples; the prefecture became well governed. He also strengthened filial devotion and righteousness to improve local customs, and made agreements and pledges clear to reinforce both benevolence and authority. At that time, thirty thousand troops stationed in the city had been short of food for half a month. He promptly exchanged salt for rice and successfully relieved their shortage. When the commanding general treated the bandits lightly and brought suffering upon the people, Zhang seized the general’s gate attendant and reprimanded him in the courtyard; that very day, the general dispatched troops in response. That the Two Chuan regions ultimately became peaceful and well governed was due to Zhang Yong’s efforts. Those who discussed his heroic deeds and exceptional administration commended them.
Li Deyu attended to military preparations without neglecting civil virtue; Zhang Yong cultivated civil government without neglecting military affairs. Drawing upon both civil and military means, applying them in turn as circumstances required—these were methods already tested by the two men. If adopted and put into practice, could they be unsuitable today? Yet, in my humble view, we lack men such as Wenrao [Li Deyu] and Zhongding [Zhang Yong]. If we truly had such men, how could government fail to be carried out? My family has lived in Shu for generations. My affections are bound to my native place, and these matters touch my own household closely. As for this modest insight, a sense of duty will not permit me to remain silent…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
安敢褎裒佯對以虛我執事明問而重貽
鄉上之辱
punctuated: 安敢褎裒佯對，以虛我執事明問，而重貽鄉上之辱？
translation_en: …how would I dare offer a pretentious, insincere reply [?], leaving Your Honor’s discerning inquiry unanswered and bringing further disgrace upon my native place [?]?

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
四川鄉試錄後序
嘉靖庚子秋四川省試事巡
按監察御史王〔珩〕實主之録
既竣〔繼〕〔興〕當敘諸卒簡致忠
告焉迺作而言曰諸士其懋
聽之哉惟兹録之作也有責
實之意焉有詢事之義焉有
===
師師之風焉僉曰録録其名
耳於實何居録録其詞耳於
事何取登名若詞萃且渙矣
安在其師師也噫嘻録其名
者爲其士之賢而録之也士
而能賢實斯稱焉耳録其言
者爲其事之協而録之也事
punctuated:
四川鄉試錄後序

嘉靖庚子秋，四川省試事，巡按監察御史王〔珩〕實主之。録既竣，〔繼〕〔興〕當敘諸卒簡，致忠告焉，迺作而言曰：「諸士其懋聽之哉！惟兹録之作也，有責實之意焉，有詢事之義焉，有師師之風焉。」僉曰：「録，録其名耳，於實何居？録，録其詞耳，於事何取？登名若詞，萃且渙矣，安在其師師也？」噫嘻！録其名者，爲其士之賢而録之也；士而能賢，實斯稱焉耳。録其言者，爲其事之協而録之也；事
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Sichuan Provincial Examination

In the autumn of the gengzi year of Jiajing [1540], Wang Heng 王珩, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, presided over the provincial examination in Sichuan. Once the record was completed, Jixing [?; 〔繼〕〔興〕] was to supply a postface on its concluding leaves and offer earnest counsel. He therefore rose and said: “Gentlemen, listen attentively! The making of this record embodies an intention to demand substance, a purpose of examining deeds, and a spirit of learning from one another.”

They all said: “A record merely records their names: what bearing does it have on substance? A record merely records their compositions: what does it draw from deeds? Their names and compositions are entered, yet they gather and then disperse. Where is this learning from one another?”

Ah! Their names are recorded because these scholars are worthy. If a scholar can indeed be worthy, his substance matches his name, and that is all. Their words are recorded because their deeds accord with them. As for their deeds …

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
而不悖言斯稱焉耳士而與
尚友之志則古今上下有神
交焉況竝肩而立者哉是必
有向往思齊交相益焉者也
蜀故多儁才迺今涵濡
聖天子作人之化濟濟蔚興環列
侍從以羽翼我
===
國家文明之治者可數也茲舉
也實惟諸士彙征之始將惟
曰吾而得第是科也若名與
氏則既列於儒紳矣而宅心
體行爲國之楨者其敢負邪
又惟曰吾而誦聖賢談古昔
陳世務洋洋浩浩則既以言
punctuated:
而不悖，言斯稱焉耳。士而與尚友之志，則古今上下有神交焉，況竝肩而立者哉！是必有向往思齊、交相益焉者也。

蜀故多儁才，迺今涵濡聖天子作人之化，濟濟蔚興，環列侍從，以羽翼我國家文明之治者可數也。茲舉也，實惟諸士彙征之始。將惟曰：「吾而得第是科也，若名與氏，則既列於儒紳矣；而宅心體行，爲國之楨者，其敢負邪？」又惟曰：「吾而誦聖賢，談古昔，陳世務，洋洋浩浩，則既以言
translation_en:
…and are not at variance, only then do their words merit that designation. If scholars possess the aspiration to befriend the worthy of the past [?], they may commune in spirit with those above and below them across ancient and modern times—how much more with those standing shoulder to shoulder with them! Surely they will admire one another, seek to equal the worthy, and benefit one another.

Shu has long abounded in outstanding talent. Now, nurtured by the sage Son of Heaven’s transforming influence in cultivating men of worth, they flourish in impressive numbers. One can enumerate those who stand among the imperial attendants, assisting our dynasty’s enlightened governance. This examination is indeed only the beginning of these scholars’ advance together. They should reflect: “Having passed this examination, my name and surname are already enrolled among the learned gentry. Yet in setting my heart aright and embodying my principles in conduct, so as to become a pillar of the state, dare I fall short?” They should also reflect: “I recite the teachings of the sages and worthies, discuss antiquity, and expound the affairs of the age in abundant and expansive language; thus already, through my words…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
進矣而樹勳篤烈爲言之徵
者其敢負邪又惟曰吾而從
俊造之選拔十得二而幸得
與焉行將被
大廷晉接之榮其必能同心體
國敷素蘊以致之民則翕受
協恭之治庶其在此其誰敢
===
孤
明時邪是實吾儕所望於二三
子之意如其徒綴空言幸一
日之捷遂將騁雲路爲身謀
利交而心變志遂而智昏則
實之不立名實弊之事而弗
稽言實愧之衷而弗協朋實
punctuated: 進矣，而樹勳篤烈爲言之徵者，其敢負邪？又惟曰：「吾而從俊造之選，拔十得二，而幸得與焉，行將被大廷晉接之榮，其必能同心體國，敷素蘊以致之民，則翕受協恭之治，庶其在此，其誰敢孤明時邪？」是實吾儕所望於二三子之意。如其徒綴空言，幸一日之捷，遂將騁雲路，爲身謀，利交而心變，志遂而智昏，則實之不立，名實弊之；事而弗稽，言實愧之；衷而弗協，朋實
translation_en: …advanced through words; but would I dare fail to establish meritorious achievements and substantial accomplishments as proof of those words? Again, each should reflect: “I have undergone the selection of outstanding talent, in which two are chosen out of ten, and have fortunately been included. Soon I shall receive the honor of being received at the imperial court. Surely we must unite in purpose and devote ourselves to the state, bringing forth our accumulated learning to benefit the people. A government that embraces all and unites them in reverent service may thus be realized. Who would dare disappoint this enlightened age?” Such, indeed, are the hopes we place in you gentlemen. If, however, you merely string together empty words and, fortunate enough to achieve a single day’s success, then race along the lofty path of official advancement to pursue your own interests, letting your hearts change when profit presents itself and your judgment grow clouded when your ambitions are fulfilled, then, if substance is not established, reputation will indeed prove your undoing; if your words are not tested against deeds, they will indeed bring you shame; if your innermost intentions are not in accord, your peers will indeed…

title: 嘉靖十九年四川鄉試錄
text:
恥之其爲斯錄也不有憂哉
爾多士其慎圖之
河南開封府歸德州儒學學
正石〔繼 典〕謹序
punctuated:
恥之，其爲斯錄也，不有憂哉？爾多士，其慎圖之！
河南開封府歸德州儒學學正石〔繼 典〕謹序。
translation_en:
…be ashamed of him. Would this not give cause for concern in compiling this record? You assembled scholars, consider this carefully!
Respectfully prefaced by Shi Jidian 石繼典, Instructor in the Confucian School of Guide Subprefecture, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan.
